## Detection Accuracy Overview {#detect_metrics_form}

we'll make a function that uses the following input data parameters to match predicted trees with validation/reference trees:

* `pred_data`: predicted data point locations as `sf` data
* `ref_data`: reference/validation/ground truth data point locations as `sf` data
* `max_dist_m`: radius of search for matching
* `max_height_error_m`: maximum allowable difference in height for to be considered correct match

for work in ponderosa pine forests, we generally set the `max_dist_m` to a 3 m radius to account for tree lean and slight horizontal misalignment in GPS data collection with 3 m representing the crown radius of a mature tree. we also typically set the `max_height_error_m` to 2 m for ponderosa pine evaluation but will need to reduce here to account for shorter trees

information used to inform the definition of "typical" crown width can be found in:

* [Gill et al. 2000](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0378-1127(99)00113-9)
* [Bechtold 2003](https://doi.org/10.1093/sjaf/27.4.269)
* [Bechtold 2004](https://doi.org/10.1093/wjaf/19.4.245)
* [Purves et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000870)

Then, we'll aggregate the instance matching results to evaluate omission rate (false negative rate or miss rate), commission rate (false positive rate), precision, recall (detection rate), and the F-score metric. As a reminder, true positive (TP) instances correctly match ground truth instances with a prediction, commission predictions do not match a ground truth instance (false positive; FP), and omissions are ground truth instances for which no predictions match (false negative; FN)

$$\textrm{omission rate} = \frac{FN}{TP+FN}$$

$$\textrm{commission rate} = \frac{FP}{TP+FP}$$

$$\textrm{precision} = \frac{TP}{TP+FP}$$

$$\textrm{recall} = \frac{TP}{TP+FN}$$

$$
\textrm{F-score} = 2 \times \frac{\bigl(precision \times recall \bigr)}{\bigl(precision + recall \bigr)}
$$


```{r}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# check df function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
validate_df_fn <- function(data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = F) {
  # check data
  if(!inherits(data,"sf") && !inherits(data,"sfc")){stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")}
  if(
    !all( sf::st_is(data, c("POINT")) )
  ){
    stop("all input data requires POINT sf data")
  }
  # names
  # uses base::setdiff and base::names
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
  
  if(length(missing_cols) > 0){
    stop("all input data requires columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  # numeric
  if(check_numeric){
    non_numeric <- data %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_cols)) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ !is.numeric(.x))) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything()) %>%
      dplyr::filter(value == TRUE)

    if (nrow(non_numeric) > 0) {
      stop("columns must be numeric: ", paste(non_numeric$name, collapse = ", "))
    }
  }
  
  # is.na() catches both NA and NaN; is.infinite() catches Inf
  invalid_dta <- data %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(required_cols)
        , ~ sum(is.na(.x) | is.infinite(.x))
      )
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::everything()
      , names_to = "column"
      , values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(count > 0)

  if (nrow(invalid_dta) > 0) {
    bad_cols <- paste(invalid_dta$column, collapse = ", ")
    stop("invalid values (NA, NaN, or Inf) found in: ", bad_cols)
  }
  return(TRUE)
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# match function
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
reference_prediction_match <- function(
  pred_data
  , ref_data
  , max_dist_m
  , max_height_error_m
) {
  #######################################################################
  # threshold checks
  #######################################################################
  if(
    any(is.na(max_dist_m)) || 
    any(is.null(max_dist_m)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_dist_m),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_dist_m` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_dist_m <- as.numeric(max_dist_m)[1]}
  if(
    any(is.na(max_height_error_m)) || 
    any(is.null(max_height_error_m)) || 
    !inherits(as.numeric(max_height_error_m),"numeric")
  ){
    stop("`max_height_error_m` must be numeric and not missing")
  }else{max_height_error_m <- as.numeric(max_height_error_m)[1]}
  #######################################################################
  # data checks
  #######################################################################
  if(nrow(pred_data)==0 | nrow(ref_data)==0){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    # return(NULL)
    
    if(nrow(pred_data)!=0){
      validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          ref_match_idx = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_height_diff_m= as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , ref_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{pred_data <- NULL}
    
    if(nrow(ref_data)!=0){
      validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
      # sort to start with largest
      ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
        dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
        # add columns
        dplyr::mutate(
          pred_match_idx = 0
          , pred_match_height_diff_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_tree_height_m = as.numeric(NA)
          , pred_match_dist_m = as.numeric(NA)
        )
    }else{ref_data <- NULL}
    # return
    return(list(
      ref_data = ref_data
      , pred_data = pred_data
    ))
  }
  
  validate_df_fn(data = pred_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  validate_df_fn(data = ref_data, required_cols = c("tree_height_m"), check_numeric = T)
  
  # proj
  if(!identical(
    sf::st_crs(pred_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
    , sf::st_crs(ref_data, parameters = T)[["epsg"]]
  )){stop("data must have same projection. see `sf::st_crs()`")}
  # sort to start with largest
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(pred_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  ref_data <- ref_data %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(desc(tree_height_m)) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(ref_match_idx = dplyr::row_number())
  #######################################################################
  # build a 2D kd-tree
  #######################################################################
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the predicted to build the tree.
    pred_coords_temp <- 
      pred_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    # Use the X and Y coordinates of the reference to build the tree.
    ref_coords_temp <- 
      ref_data %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        X = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1] %>% as.numeric()
        , Y = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2] %>% as.numeric()
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry()
    
    # perform a fixed-radius search using RANN::nn2
    nn_ans_temp <- RANN::nn2(
      # the point cloud xy data (builds the kd-tree on this)
      data = pred_coords_temp
      # the seed point xy data (number of columns must be the same as data)
      , query = ref_coords_temp
      # maximum number of neighbors to find per query
      , k = min(nrow(pred_coords_temp),nrow(ref_coords_temp))
      # the search radius (rcyl)
      , radius = max_dist_m
      , searchtype = "radius"
    )
    # huh?
    # nn_ans_temp %>% class()
    # nn_ans_temp %>% names()
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.idx %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% nrow()
    # nrow(ref_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists %>% ncol()
    # nrow(pred_coords_temp)
    # nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[1:11,] %>% dplyr::as_tibble() %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  #######################################################################  
  # iterate through the kd-tree to make matches
  #######################################################################
    if(nrow(ref_coords_temp)!=nrow(ref_data)){stop("bad kd-tree")}
    # add pred match tracker
    ref_data$pred_match_idx <- 0
    ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_tree_height_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    ref_data$pred_match_dist_m <- as.numeric(NA)
    for(i in 1:nrow(ref_coords_temp)){
      # get indices of points in the current cylinder (0 means no point found)
      nn_idx_pts <- nn_ans_temp$nn.idx[i, ]
      cyl_pts <- nn_idx_pts[nn_idx_pts > 0] 
      # remove already matched
      cyl_pts <- cyl_pts[!(cyl_pts %in% ref_data$pred_match_idx)] 
      # if available matches
      if(dplyr::coalesce(length(cyl_pts),0) >= 1) {
        # get heights
        # ref_data %>% dplyr::select(field_tree_id, tree_height_m) %>% dplyr::glimpse()
        # ref_data$tree_height_m[i]
        # pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts]
        ht_diffs <- abs(ref_data$tree_height_m[i]-pred_data$tree_height_m[cyl_pts])
        # get the minimum value among elements below the threshold
        min_val <- min(ht_diffs[ht_diffs <= max_height_error_m], na.rm = T)
        # if not none within threshold
        if(!is.infinite(min_val)){
          # the index of that value in the original full vector
          cyl_idx <- which(ht_diffs == min_val)[1] # if multiple matches, takes the nearest
          match_idx <- cyl_pts[cyl_idx]
          # distance
          nn_dist_idx <- which(nn_idx_pts == match_idx)
          nn_dist <- nn_ans_temp$nn.dists[i,nn_dist_idx]
          # update match
          ref_data$pred_match_height_diff_m[i] <- min_val
          ref_data$pred_tree_height_m[i] <- pred_data$tree_height_m[match_idx]
          ref_data$pred_match_idx[i] <- match_idx
          ref_data$pred_match_dist_m[i] <- nn_dist
          
        }
      }
    }
  #######################################################################
  # add ref id to pred and return
  #######################################################################
  # pred_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # ref_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  pred_data <- pred_data %>% 
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "pred_match_height_diff_m"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      , "ref_tree_height_m"
      , "ref_match_idx"
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      ref_data %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(ref_match_idx, pred_match_idx, pred_match_height_diff_m, pred_match_dist_m, tree_height_m) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(ref_tree_height_m=tree_height_m)
      , by = "pred_match_idx"
    )
  return(list(
    ref_data = ref_data
    , pred_data = pred_data
  ))
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# combine match to classify reference/predictions
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
ground_truth_prediction_match <- function(
  reference_prediction_match_ans
  , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m")
) {
  # check for missing both missing
  if(
    is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)
    && is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)
  ){
    warning("no data so...?????")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # if reference but no predictions...they are all omissions (FN)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  # if predictions but no reference...they are all commissions (FP)
  if(is.null(reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data)){
    return_df <-
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
        "ref_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_idx"
        , "pred_match_dist_m"
        # , "pred_tree_height_m"
        # , "tree_height_m"
        , comp_cols
      ))) %>% 
      dplyr::rename_with(
        .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
        , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    # make match_grp factor
    return_df <- return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = factor(
          match_grp
          , ordered = T
          , levels = c(
            "true positive"
            , "commission"
            , "omission"
          )
        ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
      )
    return(return_df)
  }
  
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  ############# otherwise: nrow(ref_data)>0 & nrow(pred_data)>0
  # check for comparison cols
  comp_cols <- 
    comp_cols %>% 
    # remove whitespace
    stringr::str_trim() %>% 
    # keep only those with a value
    stringr::str_subset(".")
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
    validate_df_fn(data = reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data, required_cols = comp_cols, check_numeric = T)
  }
  # tp matches
  return_df <-
    reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx!=0 & !is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
      "ref_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_idx"
      , "pred_match_dist_m"
      # , "pred_tree_height_m"
      # , "tree_height_m"
      , comp_cols
    ))) %>% 
    dplyr::rename_with(
      .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
      , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
    # add on pred geom
    dplyr::inner_join(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry()
      , by = "ref_match_idx"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "true positive")
  
  # add omissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$ref_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(pred_match_idx==0 | is.na(pred_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("ref_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_set_geometry("ref_geometry") %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "omission")
    )
    
  # add commissions
  return_df <-
    return_df %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows(
      reference_prediction_match_ans$pred_data %>%
        dplyr::filter(ref_match_idx==0 | is.na(ref_match_idx)) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(
          "ref_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_idx"
          , "pred_match_dist_m"
          # , "pred_tree_height_m"
          # , "tree_height_m"
          , comp_cols
        ))) %>% 
        dplyr::rename_with(
          .cols = dplyr::all_of(comp_cols)
          , .fn = ~paste0("pred_", .x, recycle0 = T)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(pred_geometry = sf::st_geometry(.)) %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(match_grp = "commission")
    )
  
  # make match_grp factor
  return_df <- return_df %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      match_grp = factor(
        match_grp
        , ordered = T
        , levels = c(
          "true positive"
          , "commission"
          , "omission"
        )
      ) %>% forcats::fct_rev()
    )
  
  
  if(inherits(comp_cols, "character") && length(comp_cols) > 0){
    # add a tiny value (eps) to the denominator for pct_diff_ 
    # calcs to prevent division by zero...where pct_diff_ is used for MAPE summary
    eps <- 1e-5
    return_df <- 
      return_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        # 'diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value
        dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          , .fns = ~ base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")) - .x
          , .names = "diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
        # 'pct_diff_' columns are calculated as the actual value minus the predicted value divided by the actual value
        , dplyr::across(
          .cols = paste0(
            "ref_"
            , comp_cols # c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm")
            , recycle0 = T
          )
          # 
          , .fns = ~ (.x-base::get(stringr::str_replace(dplyr::cur_column(), "^ref_", "pred_")))/(.x + eps)
          , .names = "pct_diff_{stringr::str_remove(.col, '^ref_')}"
        )
      ) 
  }
  # return
  if(nrow(return_df)==0){
    warning("no records found for ground truth to predition matching")
    return(NULL)
  }else{
    return(return_df)
  }
  
}
```

take that thing for a spin for a single plot.

)

the `ground_truth_prediction_match()` uses the output from `reference_prediction_match()` and creates a nice, clean data frame with the instances classified as TP, FP, or FN for use in aggregating to calculate detection accuracy metrics. Optionally, users can set the foundation for physical measurement accuracy assessment via the `comp_cols` argument (see the `diff_*` and `pct_diff_*` columns in the output)

  , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm", "tree_cbh_m")
)

### Example: Detection Accuracy

let's make a function to calculate the [detection accuracy metrics](#detect_metrics_form) based on aggregated TP, FP, and FN counts

```{r}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# first function takes df with cols tp_n, fp_n, and fn_n to calculate rates
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
confusion_matrix_scores_fn <- function(df) {
  df %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    omission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 1 # every single actual tree was missed
      , dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fn_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    ) # False Negative Rate or Miss Rate
    , commission_rate = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 0 # if no predictions are made, the model could not have made any commission errors
      , dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ fp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    ) # False Positive Rate
    , precision = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if no predictions are made, the model made zero incorrect positive claims
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fp_n,0) > 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fp_n)
    )
    , recall = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) == 0 ~ 1 # if there are no actual trees, there is nothing to miss
      , dplyr::coalesce(tp_n,0) == 0 & dplyr::coalesce(fn_n,0) > 0 ~ 0 # every single actual tree was missed
      , T ~ tp_n/(tp_n+fn_n)
    )
    , f_score = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(precision,0) == 0 | dplyr::coalesce(recall,0) == 0 ~ 0
      , T ~ 2 * ( (precision*recall)/(precision+recall) )
    )    
  ) 
}
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
# aggregate results from ground_truth_prediction_match()
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
###############################################################
agg_ground_truth_match <- function(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) {
  if(nrow(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans)==0){return(NULL)}
  if( !(names(ground_truth_prediction_match_ans) %>% stringr::str_equal("match_grp") %>% any()) ){stop("ground_truth_prediction_match_ans must contain `match_grp` column")}
  
  # check for difference columns (contains "_diff") and calc rmse for only those to return a single line df with colums for each diff_rmse
    if(
      (ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(tidyselect::starts_with("diff_") | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")) %>% 
        ncol() )>0
    ){
      # get rmse and mean difference/error for all columns with "_diff" but not "pct_diff"
      # get mape for all columns with "pct_diff" but not "diff_"
      rmse_df <- 
        ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::select(
          tidyselect::starts_with("diff_")
          | tidyselect::starts_with("pct_diff_")
        ) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), values_drop_na = T) %>% 
        dplyr::group_by(name) %>% 
        dplyr::summarise(
          sq = sum(value^2, na.rm = T)
          , mean = mean(value, na.rm = T)
          , sumabs = sum(abs(value), na.rm = T)
          , nomiss = sum(!is.na(value))
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sqrt(sq/nomiss)
          )
          , mape = dplyr::case_when(
            dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ sumabs/nomiss
          )
        ) %>% 
        # NA nonsense values
        dplyr::mutate(
          mape = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ mape
            , T ~ as.numeric(NA)
          )
          , rmse = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ rmse
          )
          , mean = dplyr::case_when(
            stringr::str_starts(name, "pct_diff_") ~ as.numeric(NA)
            , T ~ mean
          )
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::select(name,rmse,mean,mape) %>% 
        tidyr::pivot_wider(
          names_from = name
          , values_from = c(rmse,mean,mape)
          , names_glue = "{name}_{.value}"
        ) %>% 
        # remove columns with NA in all rows
        dplyr::select( dplyr::where( ~!all(is.na(.x)) ) )
      
      if(
        dplyr::coalesce(nrow(rmse_df),0)==0
        || dplyr::coalesce(ncol(rmse_df),0)==0
      ){
        # empty df
        rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
      }
    }else{
      # empty df
      rmse_df <- dplyr::tibble()
    }
  
  # count by match group
    agg <-
      ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::count(match_grp) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_grp = dplyr::recode_values(
          match_grp
          , "true positive"~"tp"
          , "commission"~"fp"
          , "omission"~"fn"
        )
      )
    # true positive, false positive, false negative rates
    return_df <- dplyr::tibble(match_grp = c("tp","fp","fn")) %>% 
      dplyr::left_join(agg, by = "match_grp") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(.cols = c(n), .fn = ~dplyr::coalesce(.x,0))) %>% 
      tidyr::pivot_wider(
        names_from = match_grp
        , values_from = c(n)
        , names_glue = "{match_grp}_{.value}"
      )
    # rates, precision, recall, f-score
    return_df <- confusion_matrix_scores_fn(return_df)
    # add rmse
    if(nrow(rmse_df)>0){
      return_df <- return_df %>% dplyr::bind_cols(rmse_df)
    }
  # return
  return(return_df)
}
```

## Physical Measurement Accuracy Overview {#quant_metrics_form}

Physical measurement accuracy metrics such as RMSE, MAPE, and Mean Error of tree form measurements (e.g. height, diameter) are calculated by aggregating the differences between the estimated tree attributes and the field reference values for instances classified as True Positives. These metrics tell us about the method's ability to accurately quantify the form of the trees it successfully identified.

to prepare our results for analysis, we will develop a function that aggregates the tree-level data into a single record for each metric-error measurement combination. this function will calculate detection performance metrics such as F-score, precision, and recall (using the `confusion_matrix_scores_fn()` we defined above), as well as physical measurement accuracy metrics including Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Error (ME), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) to assess the accuracy of our tree form measurements. this could be a valuable function for any future analysis comparing predictions to reference data.

here are the physical measurement accuracy metric formulas:

$$
\textrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{ \frac{  \sum_{i=1}^{N} (y_{i} - \hat{y_{i}})^{2}}{N}}
$$


$$
\textrm{ME} = \frac{  \sum_{i=1}^{N} (\hat{y_{i}} - y_{i})}{N}
$$


$$
\textrm{MAPE} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left| \frac{y_{i} - \hat{y_{i}}}{y_{i}} \right|
$$

Where $N$ is equal to the total number of correctly matched trees, $y_i$ is the ground truth measured value and $\hat{y_i}$ is the predicted value of $i$

There is a lot going on in our `agg_ground_truth_match()` function but it's application is straightforward enough:

* The minimum required input is a data frame of the raw instance matches with a column named `match_grp` which is string/factor with the levels "true positive", "commission", and "omission" as returned by the `ground_truth_prediction_match()` function
* Optionally, if the data contain columns with the prefix "diff_" the mean error (ME) is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix "_mean" and the RMSE is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix "_rmse"
  - interpretation of the ME is enhanced if these "diff_" columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value (e.g. `pred_diameter_m - gt_diameter_m`) 
* Optionally, if the data contain columns with the prefix "pct_diff_" the mean absolute percent error (MAPE) is calculated for those columns with the return having the suffix "_mape"
  - these "pct_diff_" columns are calculated as the actual value minus the predicted value divided by the actual value (e.g. `(gt_diameter_m - pred_diameter_m)/gt_diameter_m`) 
  
### Example: Physical measurement Accuracy

we already demonstrated minimum use of the `agg_ground_truth_match()` function to get detection accuracy metrics, now we'll demonstrate the physical measurement accuracy metrics by keeping the `diff_*` and `pct_diff_*` columns calculated with the `ground_truth_prediction_match()` function

# test a bunch of different variable window sizes within `lidR::lmf()` 
# that cover a range of possibilities and function shapes including linear, concave up, and concave down
# empty list
vws_functions <- list()
min_ws_temp <- 0.5
max_ws_temp <- 6.0

n_temp <- 40
# end points for the line
linear_targets <- base::seq(from = max_ws_temp, to = max_ws_temp*2*10, length.out = n_temp)

for (i in 1:n_temp) {
  target_height <- linear_targets[i]
  slope <- (max_ws_temp - min_ws_temp) / target_height
  
  # Pad names with a zero (01 to 60) for clean sorting
  func_name <- base::paste0("linear_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
  
  v_min  <- base::as.numeric(min_ws_temp)
  v_max  <- base::as.numeric(max_ws_temp)
  v_slope <- base::as.numeric(slope)
  
  func_body <- base::substitute(
    dplyr::case_when(
      base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
      (v_min + v_slope * x) < v_min ~ v_min,
      (v_min + v_slope * x) > v_max ~ v_max,
      TRUE ~ (v_min + v_slope * x)
    ),
    list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_slope = v_slope)
  )
  
  vws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
}
vws_functions[1]
vws_functions[[1]]
class(vws_functions[[1]])
vws_functions[[1]](1.5)
vws_functions[[1]](0)
vws_functions[[1]](18)

vws_functions[[40]](1.5)
vws_functions[[40]](0)
vws_functions[[40]](18)

# --- Concave Down / Saturating Functions (30 unique variations) ---
# total potential growth (or distance) between the floor and the ceiling is: 6.0-0.5=5.5
# the halfway point of growth is exactly half of that distance: 5.5/2=2.75
# when the curve reaches its exact halfway point, the resulting window size must be the baseline floor plus that half-distance: 0.5+2.75=3.25
# in `half_sat`, setting the constant of 1.375 means the function will hit its halfway mark of 3.25 when the tree is only 1.375 meters tall
  # max slope = 4 (for ever 1 m growth, ws increases by 4 m)
  # 4 = (6.0-0.5)/c >> 4 = 5.5/c >> c = 5.5/4 >> c = 1.375
# how far out to look based on maximum plot/tree height? 45 m tree??
n_temp <- 30
for (i in 1:n_temp) {
  c <- 1.375 # ~dbh height
  max_end <- 45 # biggest tree everrrrr
  half_sat <- c + (i - 1) * ( (max_end-c) / (n_temp-1))
  
  func_name <- base::paste0("concave_down_", base::sprintf("%02d", i))
  
  v_min  <- base::as.numeric(min_ws_temp)
  v_max  <- base::as.numeric(max_ws_temp)
  v_half <- base::as.numeric(half_sat)
  
  func_body <- base::substitute(
    dplyr::case_when(
      base::is.na(x) ~ v_min,
      (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x)) < v_min ~ v_min,
      (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x)) > v_max ~ v_max,
      TRUE ~ (v_min + ((v_max - v_min) * x) / (v_half + x))
    ),
    list(v_min = v_min, v_max = v_max, v_half = v_half)
  )
  
  vws_functions[[func_name]] <- base::as.function(c(base::alist(x = ), func_body))
}

        , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm") #, "tree_cbh_m")
      )
      
      if(!is.null(rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data) && nrow(rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data)>0){
        gt_temp <- gt_temp %>% 
          # remove FP that were outside boundary since we included them to allow for edge reference trees to be matched
          dplyr::left_join(
            rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data %>% 
              sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
              dplyr::select(pred_match_idx, is_in_stand)
            , by = "pred_match_idx"
          ) %>% 
          dplyr::filter(
            !(!is_in_stand & match_grp=="commission")
          ) 
      }
      # gt_temp %>% agg_ground_truth_match() %>% dplyr::glimpse()
      return(gt_temp)
  })
  xxx_ground_truth_prediction_match_ans <- 
    xxx_gt_pred_match_map_ans %>%
    purrr::compact() %>% 
    purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "plot")
  ans <- xxx_ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    agg_ground_truth_match()
  ans %>% readr::write_csv(file.path("../data/testtest", paste0(nm,".csv")))
  return(ans)
}

## Implement Accuracy Evaluation

because we have plot-level reference field data but a complete census of predictions, we need to perform accuracy evaluation for each plot and then aggregate to the entire study site. 

let's perform instance matching over each plot and then bring those results together after

```{r}
# make a temp function to map over each plot
inst_match_fn_temp <- function(plt_id) {
  # reference_prediction_match
  rp_match_ans_temp <- reference_prediction_match(
    pred_data = 
      treetops_sf %>% 
        dplyr::filter(tree_height_m>=min_tree_ht_m) %>% 
        sf::st_intersection(
          validation_plots %>% 
            dplyr::filter(plot==plt_id) %>%  
            dplyr::mutate(plot_radius_m = plot_radius_m+1) %>% # 1 = 0.5*max_dist_m where max_dist_m=allowable search distance for TP match
            sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
            sf::st_buffer(.$plot_radius_m) %>% 
            dplyr::select(plot_area_m2)
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::left_join(
          treetops_sf %>% 
            # clip to study boundary
            sf::st_intersection(
              validation_plots %>% 
                dplyr::filter(plot==plt_id) %>%  
                sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
                sf::st_buffer(.$plot_radius_m) %>% 
                dplyr::mutate(is_in_stand = T)
            ) %>% 
            sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
            dplyr::select(treeID, is_in_stand)
          , by = "treeID"
        ) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          is_in_stand = dplyr::coalesce(is_in_stand,F)
        )
    , ref_data = 
      validation_trees %>% 
        dplyr::filter(plot==plt_id) %>%
        dplyr::rename(tree_height_m=height_m, dbh_cm=dbh_cm, tree_cbh_m=cbh_m) %>% 
        sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf))
    , max_dist_m = 2 # round(median(validation_trees$crown_width_m)/2)
    , max_height_error_m = 1.5 # round(sd(validation_trees$height_m)*1.1,1)
  )
  # # wha?
  # rp_match_ans_temp$ref_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  # rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  
  gt_temp <- ground_truth_prediction_match(
    reference_prediction_match_ans = rp_match_ans_temp
    , comp_cols = c("tree_height_m", "dbh_cm") #, "tree_cbh_m")
  )
  
  if(!is.null(rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data) && nrow(rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data)>0){
    gt_temp <- gt_temp %>% 
      # remove FP that were outside boundary since we included them to allow for edge reference trees to be matched
      dplyr::left_join(
        rp_match_ans_temp$pred_data %>% 
          sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
          dplyr::select(pred_match_idx, is_in_stand)
        , by = "pred_match_idx"
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::filter(
        !(!is_in_stand & match_grp=="commission")
      ) 
  }
  # gt_temp %>% agg_ground_truth_match() %>% dplyr::glimpse()
  return(gt_temp)
}

## Detection Accuracy Results{#detect_acc_res}

first, we'll check out the site-wide detection accuracy results

what if we look at the detection accuracy results by treatment type?

    which_dta <-

```

interesting to see the variation in detection accuracy across the different treatment types. the more aggressive treatments (i.e. treatments that removed more trees and left fewer residual trees) have a smaller margin for error with respect to tree detection accuracy since each tree carries more weight. however, the more open stand conditions created by the more aggressive treatments should make it easier to detect each individual if they are spaced with openings between individuals. at the same time the units with a high proportion of slash piles might result in increased commission rate (i.e. higher number of false positive tree predictions) even though we applied a slash pile mask. an additional data check may be needed for the remaining trees to check whether or not they are "green" while it is not clear if only live or both dead and live trees were sampled during the field inventory. and many, many more questions...

let's see the relationship between tree detection (recall rate) and tree height within each flight. we'll look at true positive and omissions (FN) and use the field-measured tree height to quantify the proportion of trees within a height bin that were detected by the UAS method

```{r}
# make ggplot2::cut_* bins pretty
make_bins_pretty <- function(bin_factor, suffix = "") {
  # convert factor to character and remove brackets and parens
  clean_labels <- bin_factor %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all(c("\\[" = "", "\\(" = "", "\\]" = "", "\\)" = "")) %>%
    stringr::str_replace(",", "-")
  
  # suffix
  if(stringr::str_squish(suffix) != "" && inherits(suffix,"character")){
    clean_labels <- stringr::str_c(clean_labels, " ", suffix) %>% stringr::str_squish()
  }
  
  # reorder based on the original factor levels 
  forcats::fct_reorder(factor(clean_labels), as.numeric(bin_factor))
}

ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(match_grp %in% c("true positive","omission")) %>% 
  # dplyr::glimpse()
  # metric cuts/bins
  dplyr::mutate(
    tree_height_m_bin = ggplot2::cut_width(ref_tree_height_m, width = 3, boundary = 0, closed = "left") %>% 
      make_bins_pretty(suffix = "m") %>% 
      forcats::fct_relabel(~ stringr::str_replace(.x, "^0-", paste0(min_tree_ht_m,"-")) )
    , is_detected = match_grp %in% c("true positive")
    , is_detected = as.numeric(is_detected)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::count(match_grp, tree_height_m_bin) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(tree_height_m_bin) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(pct = n/sum(n,na.rm = T)) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    lab = ifelse(
      pct>0.095
      , paste0(
        scales::percent(pct,accuracy=1) 
        ,"\n("
        , scales::comma(n,accuracy=1) 
        , ")"
      )
      , ""
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  # dplyr::glimpse()
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = pct, x = tree_height_m_bin)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = match_grp)
    , width = 0.6
    , color = NA, alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(label = lab, group = match_grp, fontface = "bold", color = match_grp)
    # , color = "black"
    , size = 2.5
    , position = ggplot2::position_stack(vjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = pal_match_grp) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("white","black"), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(drop = F) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0,1,by=0.2)
    , labels = scales::percent
    , expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.02))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "tree height", y = "", fill = ""
    , subtitle = "Recall rate by tree height bin"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light()+
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "top"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
    , axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
    , axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

the trend of increasing detection rate with tree height demonstrated with this data aligns well with prior work using aerial point cloud data for single-tree forest inventories

let's look at the commission rate (commission error) by tree height using the UAS-detected tree heights to determine if our ITD variable window function could be improved

```{r, fig.height=10}
ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(match_grp %in% c("true positive","commission")) %>%

        , ")"
      )

  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  # dplyr::glimpse()
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = pct, x = tree_height_m_bin)

  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(drop = F) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0,1,by=0.2)
    , labels = scales::percent
    , expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.02))
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "tree height", y = "", fill = ""
    , subtitle = "Commission rate by tree height bin"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light()+
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "top"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
    , axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
    , axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

the commission error (percentage shown in the gray bar) is highest for the small trees which suggests we could potentially improve our ITD window function to decrease the number of trees detected in this height range. However, going back to the detection rate above, this same height range also had the lowest detection rate which would suggest we increase the number of trees identified in this height range. This conflict suggests that the trees in this height range are likely difficult to detect for the study area using the data and ITD methods used in this study. For example, they may be subordinate to directly adjacent taller trees with the crowns interlocking, so they are often grouped with the taller tree during the CHM-based ITD.

## Physical measurement Accuracy Results{#quant_acc}

let's table the tree-level aggregated measurement error

```{r}

```

UAS-measured heights are highly accurate but those DBH measurements do not align very well. perhaps this is due to the fact that DBH wasn't actually measured in the field. instead, DRC (diameter at root crown) was measured and then we converted DRC to DBH using the Chojnacky & Rogers ([1999](https://doi.org/10.1093/wjaf/14.1.14)) model...therefore, it's probably best not to view these DBH metrics as measurements of "error" but as measurements of "comparison"

and plot predicted versus reference values for correct predictions (TP)

```{r}
####################################
# area scatter
####################################
dta_temp <-
  ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>% 
  dplyr::filter(match_grp=="true positive") %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>% 
  dplyr::bind_cols(
    agg_ground_truth_match_ans %>% 
      dplyr::select(tidyselect::ends_with("_rmse") , tidyselect::ends_with("_mape"), tidyselect::ends_with("_mean") )

# plt fn temp
plt_scatter_fn <- function(
    dta
    , which_col = "dbh_cm"
    , title_lab = "DBH"
    , x_lab = "reference DBH (cm)" # latex2exp::TeX("reference area ($m^2$)")
    , y_lab = "predicted DBH (cm)" # latex2exp::TeX("predicted area ($m^2$)")
){
    d <- dta
    # construct the formula: "y_var ~ x_var"
    y_var <- paste0("pred_",which_col)
    x_var <- paste0("ref_",which_col)
    formula_obj <- stats::as.formula(
      paste( 
        y_var
        , "~"
        , x_var 
      )
    )
    lm_temp <- lm(
      formula = formula_obj
      , data = d
    )
    # summary(lm_temp)
    # scales::percent(summary(lm_temp)$r.squared, accuracy = 0.1)
    lmf_temp <- paste0(
      "y = "
      , scales::number(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[2,1], accuracy = 0.01) #slope
      , "x"
      , ifelse(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[1,1]<0," - ", " + ")
      , scales::number(abs(summary(lm_temp)$coefficients[1,1]), accuracy = 0.01) #intercept
    )
    # scale limits
    max_val <- max( 
      max(d[[y_var]],na.rm=T)
      , max(d[[x_var]],na.rm=T)
    )
    
    # annotations
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("diff_",which_col, "_rmse")) ) ){
    rmse_val <- d %>% 
      dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("diff_",which_col, "_rmse"))) %>% 
      dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
      unique()
      rmse_val <- dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_cm") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (cm)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = " (m)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m2") ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (m²)")
        , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct") ~ scales::percent(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1)
        , T ~ scales::number(rmse_val, accuracy = 0.1)
      )
    }else{rmse_val <- NA}
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("pct_diff_",which_col, "_mape")) ) ){
      mape_val <- d %>% 
        dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("pct_diff_",which_col, "_mape"))) %>% 
        dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
        unique() %>% 
        scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1)
    }else{mape_val <- NA}
    if( any( stringr::str_equal(names(d), paste0("diff_",which_col, "_mean")) ) ){
      me_val <- d %>% 
        dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
        dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(paste0("diff_",which_col, "_mean"))) %>% 
        dplyr::pull(1) %>% 
        unique()
        me_val <- dplyr::case_when(
          stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_cm") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (cm)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.01, suffix = " (m)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_m2") ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = " (m²)")
          , stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct") ~ scales::percent(me_val, accuracy = 0.1)
          , T ~ scales::number(me_val, accuracy = 0.1)
        )
    }else{me_val <- NA}
    
    # plot
    p <- d %>% 
      ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = .data[[y_var]], x = .data[[x_var]])) +
      ggplot2::geom_abline(color = "gray33", lwd = 1) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(color = "brown", alpha = 0.7, size = 0.9) +
      ggplot2::geom_smooth(lwd = 0.8, method = "lm", se=F, color = "gray", linetype = "dashed") +
      ggplot2::annotate(
        "text", 
        x = -Inf, y = Inf # Top Left
        , label = 
          # paste0(
          #   "R^2 == "
          #   , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared)*100, accuracy = 0.1)
          #   , "*'%'"
          # )
          paste0(
            "RMSE = ", rmse_val
            , ifelse(!is.na(mape_val), paste0("\nMAPE = ", mape_val),"")
            , ifelse(!is.na(me_val), paste0("\nME = ", me_val),"")
            , "\n"
            , lmf_temp
            , "\n R² = "
            # , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared)*100, accuracy = 0.1, suffix = "%")
            , scales::number((summary(lm_temp)$r.squared), accuracy = 0.01)
          )
        , hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.1
        , parse = F
        , size = 3
      ) +
      # ggplot2::facet_wrap(
      #   facets = dplyr::vars(dataset_factor), scales = "free", axis.labels = "all"
      #   # , labeller = ggplot2::labeller(class = ggplot2::label_wrap_gen(width = 10))
      # ) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = x_lab
        , y = y_lab
        # , color = "image-field\ndiameter diff."
        # , subtitle = latex2exp::TeX("bulk volume ($m^3$) comparison")
        # , subtitle = paste("Predicted", title_lab,"versus Reference", title_lab)
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_light() +
      ggplot2::theme(
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black")
      ) 
    if(stringr::str_ends(which_col,"_pct")){
      p + 
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), labels = scales::percent, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1))) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), labels = scales::percent, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1)))
    }else{
      return(
        p + 
        ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1))) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max_val ), expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1)))
      )
    }
  }

let's shift our focus to relative error (MAPE) while providing absolute context (RMSE and ME) as text or secondary metrics to look into the penalty we face due to inaccuracies in DBH for small stems. for example, a 3 cm error on a 6 cm small tree is a 50% relative error while that same 3 cm error on a 30 cm merchantable tree is a minor 10% error.

let's look into the DBH prediction error over the range of tree sizes and use LOESS smoothing to highlight the trend in relative prediction error

```{r}
# Data trends (dashed) are visualized using a LOESS (locally weighted scatterplot smoothing) regression. 
# A span of 1.0 was utilized to include 100% of the observations in each local neighborhood, 
# and the local polynomial degree was restricted to 1 (local linear regression) to prevent overfitting and boundary inflation at the data extremes.

# The dashed line represents a locally estimated scatterplot smoothing (LOESS) trend line
# , calculated with a smoothing parameter (span) of 1.0 and a local linear polynomial fit (degree = 1).
ground_truth_prediction_match_ans %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # swap the error calc
    pct_diff_dbh_cm = (pred_dbh_cm-ref_dbh_cm)/ref_dbh_cm
  ) %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(match_grp %in% c("true positive")) %>% 
  # dplyr::glimpse()
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = pct_diff_dbh_cm, x = ref_dbh_cm)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray33", lwd = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "brown", alpha = 0.7, size = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(
    method = "loess", se=F
    , span = 1 # 0.75 = default
    , method.args = list(degree = 1)
    , lwd = 1, color = "gray", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text"
    , x = Inf
    # , y = 0.045
    , y = Inf
    , label = "prediction > reference"
    , hjust = 1.1
    , vjust = 1.2
    , parse = F
    , size = 2.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text"
    , x = Inf
    # , y = -0.04
    , y = -Inf
    , label = "prediction < reference"
    , hjust = 1.1
    , vjust = -0.4
    , parse = F
    , size = 2.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n=8)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(-1,1)
    # breaks = seq(-1,1,by=0.2)
    , breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n = 8)
    , labels = scales::percent
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "field reference DBH (cm)", y = "relative DBH error"
    , subtitle = "relative DBH error (%) by reference tree DBH"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light()
```

## Stand-Level Accuracy Results{#stand_acc}

In addition to the tree-level accuracy metrics (e.g. height RMSE and MAPE), we can also calculate stand-level accuracy metrics by aggregating estimates from the reference (ground truth) and predicted trees irrespective of whether or not they were matched (i.e. true positive) during instance matching. 

*for this data, "stand-level" refers to the combined area covered by all field plots*

```{r}
# uas trees in plots
pred_trees_temp <-
  treetops_sf %>% 
  sf::st_intersection(
    validation_plots_polygons %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::summarise(
        area_m2 = sum(plot_area_m2)
        , n_plots = dplyr::n()
        , geometry = sf::st_union(.)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(terra::crs(treetops_sf))
  ) %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry()
pred_stand_temp <- 
  pred_trees_temp %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(area_m2, n_plots) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_trees = dplyr::n()
    , basal_area_m2 = sum(basal_area_m2)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    area_ha = (area_m2/10000)
    , basal_area_m2_per_ha = basal_area_m2/area_ha
    , trees_per_ha = n_trees/area_ha
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-area_m2)
# dplyr::glimpse(pred_stand_temp)
ref_stand_temp <-
  validation_trees %>% 
  sf::st_transform(terra::crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
  sf::st_intersection(
    validation_plots_polygons %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::summarise(
        area_m2 = sum(plot_area_m2)
        , n_plots = dplyr::n()
        , geometry = sf::st_union(.)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(terra::crs(treetops_sf))
  ) %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(basal_area_m2 = pi * dbh_cm^2 / (4*10000)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(area_m2, n_plots) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_trees = dplyr::n()
    , basal_area_m2 = sum(basal_area_m2)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    area_ha = (area_m2/10000)
    , basal_area_m2_per_ha = basal_area_m2/area_ha
    , trees_per_ha = n_trees/area_ha
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-area_m2)
# dplyr::glimpse(ref_stand_temp)
stand_temp <- 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    ref_stand_temp %>% dplyr::rename_with(.cols = -c(area_ha,n_plots), ~paste0("ref_",.x,recycle0 = T))
    , pred_stand_temp %>% dplyr::rename_with(.cols = -c(area_ha,n_plots), ~paste0("pred_",.x,recycle0 = T))
    , by = dplyr::join_by(area_ha,n_plots)
  ) %>% 
  # comps not done in agg_ground_truth_match()
  dplyr::mutate(
    # 'diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value
    diff_trees_per_ha = pred_trees_per_ha-ref_trees_per_ha
    , diff_basal_area_m2 = pred_basal_area_m2-ref_basal_area_m2
    , diff_basal_area_m2_per_ha = pred_basal_area_m2_per_ha-ref_basal_area_m2_per_ha
    # 'abs_diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value
    , abs_diff_trees_per_ha = abs(diff_trees_per_ha)
    , abs_diff_basal_area_m2 = abs(diff_basal_area_m2)
    , abs_diff_basal_area_m2_per_ha = abs(diff_basal_area_m2_per_ha)
    # 'pct_diff_' columns are calculated as the predicted value minus the actual value divided by the actual value
    , pct_diff_trees_per_ha = (pred_trees_per_ha-ref_trees_per_ha)/ref_trees_per_ha
    , pct_diff_basal_area_m2 = (pred_basal_area_m2-ref_basal_area_m2)/ref_basal_area_m2
    , pct_diff_basal_area_m2_per_ha = (pred_basal_area_m2_per_ha-ref_basal_area_m2_per_ha)/ref_basal_area_m2_per_ha
  )
```

Should we even be calculating basal area for pinyon-juniper systems? Traditional silvicultural metrics like basal area and volume are not particularly useful for managing these woodlands because the trees/shrubs feature highly irregular, multi-stemmed growth forms. Furthermore, field inventories like FIA measure diameter at root collar (DRC) instead of standard diameter at breast height (DBH) and then convert those metrics using regional allometric equations. Because of this, it is probably inappropriate for us to quantify the accuracy of UAS-predicted DBH, which is modeled using a height-to-DBH equation from local FIA data, against field-calculated DBH values derived from converted DRC measurements. Instead, modern management evaluations in these pinyon-juniper systems prioritize tree density measurements and canopy clump configurations to analyze structural and spatial patterns. This focus on horizontal canopy architecture, tracking trees per hectare and interspace connectivity, provides a much more direct and ecologically meaningful way to evaluate ecosystem health and fire risk across these arid landscapes.

## Canopy Cover Evaluation{#cc_eval}

Let's shift our focus to evaluating UAS-predicted canopy cover compared to field-measured values. Recall that [to obtain field-measured canopy cover](#ref_field_dta), we averaged the field-recorded horizontal crown length and width to approximate a circular diameter, used that diameter to calculate a 2D circular crown area for each tree, and determined the proportion of each plot covered by these assumed circular crowns. For each plot, we'll compare this proportion to the canopy cover predicted by the UAS using trees whose tree-top points fall within the plot boundaries irrespective of if a tree was matched as a true positive in our instance matching evaluation. Requiring the tree-top point to fall within the plot mimics the field technique of only measuring stems located inside the plot boundaries. The main caveats attached to this canopy cover accuracy evaluation are that measuring crown dimensions accurately using manual ground techniques is notoriously difficult, and the simple circular shape assumption rarely matches the irregular crown morphologies found in the real-world ([Rautiainen et al. 2008](https://doi.org/10.14214/sf.261); [Gallardo-Salazar & Pompa-García 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12244144); [Ren et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.14401)).

```{r}
# read crowns
pred_crowns_temp <- 
  cloud2trees:::search_dir_final_detected(dir = c2t_process_dir)[["crowns_flist"]] %>% 
  purrr::map(
    \(x)
    crowns_sf <- sf::st_read(
      dsn = x, quiet = TRUE
      , query = 
        sprintf(
          "SELECT * FROM %s WHERE treeID IN (%s)"
          , basename(x) %>% stringr::str_remove("^.*/") %>% stringr::str_remove("\\.[^.]+$")
          , stringr::str_c("'", unique(pred_trees_temp$treeID), "'", collapse = ", ")
        )
    ) %>% 
    cloud2trees::simplify_multipolygon_crowns()
  ) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
# pred_crowns_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# pred_trees_temp %>% nrow()
# pred_crowns_temp %>% nrow()
# attach predicted cc to plot data
validation_plots_polygons <- plot_crowns_cc_fn(
    plots_sf = validation_plots_polygons
    , crowns_sf = pred_crowns_temp
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(
    .cols = tidyselect::starts_with("canopy_")
    , ~ paste0("pred_",.x,recycle0 = T)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff_canopy_cov_pct = pred_canopy_cov_pct-ref_canopy_cov_pct
    , diff_canopy_cov_area_m2 = pred_canopy_cov_area_m2-ref_canopy_cov_area_m2
  )

# validation_plots_polygons %>% dplyr::glimpse()

let's check the relationship between the UAS and reference field plot-level canopy cover measurements

```{r}
cc_agg_temp <- validation_plots_polygons %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    sq = sum(diff_canopy_cov_pct^2, na.rm = T)
    , mean = mean(diff_canopy_cov_pct, na.rm = T)
    , sumabs = sum(abs(diff_canopy_cov_pct), na.rm = T)
    , nomiss = sum(!is.na(diff_canopy_cov_pct))
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    rmse = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::coalesce(nomiss,0)==0 ~ as.numeric(NA)
      , T ~ sqrt(sq/nomiss)
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(mean,rmse) %>% 
  dplyr::rename_with(
    ~paste0("diff_canopy_cov_pct_",.x, recycle0 = T)
  ) 
# get the plottttttttttttttttttt
validation_plots_polygons %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::bind_cols(
    cc_agg_temp    
  ) %>% 
  plt_scatter_fn(which_col = "canopy_cov_pct", title_lab = "Canopy Cover", x_lab = "reference Canopy Cover (%)", y_lab = "predicted Canopy Cover (%)")


```

The plot-level aggregation comparing the canopy cover of the field method to the UAS method yielded an RMSE of `r scales::percent(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_rmse,accuracy=0.1)` and a mean error (ME) of `r scales::percent(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_mean,accuracy=0.1)`. These values mean that the average UAS prediction of plot-level canopy cover is off by about ±`r scales::number(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_rmse*100,accuracy=0.1)` percentage points from the field-measured value which is generally considered highly accurate and operationally acceptable. The `r ifelse(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_mean>=0,"positive","negative")` ME of `r scales::percent(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_mean,accuracy=0.1)` means that, on average across all plots, the UAS method is systematically `r ifelse(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_mean>=0,"overpredicting","underpredicting")` canopy cover by `r scales::number(cc_agg_temp$diff_canopy_cov_pct_mean*100,accuracy=0.1)` percentage points compared to the field data.

The higher canopy cover predictions by the UAS method compared to the field method is a logical outcome of how crown boundaries are defined by each method. The UAS approach delineates crowns from an aerial perspective and utilizes a segmentation routine that prevents any two crowns from overlapping. Conversely, the field method assumes a perfectly circular crown extending symmetrically from the tree stem. In dense stands, this circular geometry causes field-calculated crowns to overlap in 2D space which may artificially reduce the total canopy cover. In reality, tree branches grow asymmetrically. For example, extending away from competitors to capture available sunlight. The UAS captures this irregular, outward branch expansion which may explain why it results in larger (and more realistic) canopy cover measurements than the field-based method.

let's check out a visual representation of that phenomenon by looking as some example plots

```{r, results=F, fig.show='hide'}
# harrypotter::hp(n=2, option="hermionegranger") %>% scales::show_col()
terra_plt_fn_temp <- function(rgb, rgb_square, plot_poly, ref_pt, ref_poly, pred_poly, plot_title="") {
  grDevices::dev.new()
  grDevices::dev.control("enable")
  
  terra::plotRGB(rgb)
  terra::plot(rgb_square, add = T, border = "white", col = NA, lwd = 2)
  terra::plot(terra::vect(plot_poly %>% sf::st_transform(terra::crs(rgb)) ), add = T, border = "white", col = NA, lwd = 0.8)
  terra::plot(terra::vect(ref_pt %>% sf::st_transform(terra::crs(rgb)) ), add = T, col = harrypotter::hp(n=2, option="hermionegranger")[1])
  terra::plot(terra::vect(ref_poly %>% sf::st_transform(terra::crs(rgb)) ), add = T, border = harrypotter::hp(n=2, option="hermionegranger")[1], col = NA, lwd = 1.4)
  terra::plot(terra::vect(pred_poly %>% sf::st_transform(terra::crs(rgb)) ), add = T, border = harrypotter::hp(n=2, option="hermionegranger")[2], col = NA, lwd = 1.4)
  # graphics::title(main = plot_title, cex.main = 0, col.main = "white", font.main = 2) 
  
  p <- grDevices::recordPlot()
  grDevices::dev.off()
  return(p)
}

```

interesting. we see that the UAS crowns (orange) generally align with the green areas that appear to be trees from the aerial perspective and,the individual crowns segmented using the UAS method do not overlap. By contrast, the field-measured stems and the assumed circular crowns (red) overlap with each other and are not always spatially aligned with the green areas in the aerial imagery. This slight misalignment is the result of variations in the location recording systems used on the ground and the UAS system in addition to the stems of trees not being positioned directly under the crown due to real-world tree lean. We can also see a few examples of field-measured tree stems that are very near each other so that the simulated circular crowns have high or even complete overlap.

We can move beyond summary canopy cover percentages and evaluate the spatial overlap of the crown footprints using the Intersection over Union (IoU) metric. The IoU index provides a spatial assessment by measuring the geographic alignment between the UAS crown polygons and circular field crowns. To quantify the spatial agreement between your UAS-delineated crowns and the field-calculated circular crowns, IoU is calculated by dividing the area of overlap between the two crown layers by the total combined area of both layers:

$$
\text{IoU}=\frac{\text{Area of Intersection}}{\text{Area of Union}}=\frac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}
$$

where $A$ represents the spatial footprint of the field-calculated circular crowns within a plot and $B$ represents the spatial footprint of the UAS-segmented crown polygons within the same plot.

```{r}
# validation_plots_polygons %>% dplyr::glimpse()
iou_temp <-
  1:nrow(validation_plots_polygons) %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    # plot
    plot_temp <- validation_plots_polygons %>% dplyr::slice(x)
    # ref pts
    ref_pt_temp <- validation_trees %>% dplyr::filter(plot==plot_temp$plot)
    # ref polys
    ref_poly_temp <- 
      ref_pt_temp %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(crown_radius_m=crown_diam_m/2) %>% 
      sf::st_buffer(.$crown_radius_m) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) %>% 
      sf::st_union()
    # pred polys
    pred_poly_temp <- 
      pred_crowns_temp %>% 
        dplyr::inner_join(
          treetops_sf %>% 
            sf::st_intersection(plot_temp %>% sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(treetops_sf)) ) %>% 
            sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
            dplyr::select(treeID)
          , by = "treeID"
        ) %>% 
        sf::st_union()
    u <- sf::st_union(ref_poly_temp,pred_poly_temp)
    i <- sf::st_intersection(ref_poly_temp,pred_poly_temp)
    
    return(
      plot_temp %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::select(plot) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          crown_pred_ref_iou = as.numeric(sf::st_area(i))/as.numeric(sf::st_area(u))
        )
    )
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
# add
validation_plots_polygons <- validation_plots_polygons %>% dplyr::left_join(iou_temp, by = "plot")
```

# Treatment Unit Silvicultural Summary{#silv_sum}

In this section, we're going to aggregate the UAS-detected trees within the treatment units to produce silvicultural summaries.

first, let's read in the UAS-delineated tree crown polygons as well so we have them for visualization and such

```{r do-the-crown-stuff}
# ```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE}
crowns_sf <-
  cloud2trees:::search_dir_final_detected(dir = c2t_process_dir)[["crowns_flist"]] %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    # read it
    crowns_sf_temp <- sf::st_read(
      dsn = x, quiet = TRUE
      , query = 
        sprintf(
          "SELECT * FROM %s WHERE treeID IN (%s)"
          , basename(x) %>% stringr::str_remove("^.*/") %>% stringr::str_remove("\\.[^.]+$")
          , stringr::str_c("'", unique(treetops_sf$treeID), "'", collapse = ", ")
        )
    ) %>% 
    # throw in hey_xxxxxxxxxx to test it works if we include non-existant columns
    dplyr::select( dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "treeID"
      , "crown_area_m2"
      , "crown_diameter_m"
      , "tree_height_m"
      , "tree_x"
      , "tree_y"
    )))
    # check if cols exist
    has_cols <- all(c("crown_area_m2", "crown_diameter_m") %in% names(crowns_sf_temp))
    
    if(!has_cols){
      # get the crown data
      crowns_sf_temp <- 
        crowns_sf_temp %>% 
        cloud2trees::simplify_multipolygon_crowns() %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          crown_area_m2 = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric()
        ) %>% 
        cloud2trees:::st_calculate_diameter() %>% 
        dplyr::rename(crown_diameter_m=diameter_m)
      #write....FYI: this replaces the raw data from cloud2trees and excludes trees outside of the treatment units...
      sf::st_write(obj=crowns_sf_temp, dsn = x, quiet = T, append = F)
    }
    
    # return data
    crowns_sf_temp <- crowns_sf_temp %>% 
      dplyr::select(
        treeID
        , crown_area_m2
        , crown_diameter_m
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::inner_join(
        treetops_sf %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        # throw in hey_xxxxxxxxxx to test it works if we include non-existant columns
        dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
          "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
          , "crown_area_m2"
          , "crown_diameter_m"
        )))
      )
    return(crowns_sf_temp)
    
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
# crowns_sf %>% dplyr::glimpse()
# crowns_sf %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% dplyr::count(trtmnt_type)

# add crown data to tree points
treetops_sf <- 
  treetops_sf %>% 
  # throw in hey_xxxxxxxxxx to test it works if we include non-existant columns
  dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
    "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"

## Function to Calculate Silviclutural Metrics

let's make a function to summarize the data and create common silvicultural metrics within our stand boundary

```{r}
###################################################################################
# define a function to convert columns in data frame from metric to imperial
# see: 
# https://www.forestnb.com/archives/forest-nb-news/resources/conversions/
# https://www.ars.usda.gov/is/np/agbyproducts/agbyappendix.pdf
###################################################################################
calc_imperial_units_fn <- function(df) {
  df %>% 
  # convert to imperial units
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_cm")
        , ~ .x * 0.394
        , .names = "{.col}_in"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_m")
        , ~ .x * 3.281
        , .names = "{.col}_ft"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_m2_per_ha")
        , ~ .x * 4.359
        , .names = "{.col}_ftac"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_kg_per_ha")
        , ~ .x * 0.892178
        , .names = "{.col}_lbsac"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_per_ha") & 
          !tidyselect::ends_with("_m2_per_ha") & 
          !tidyselect::ends_with("_kg_per_ha")
        , ~ .x * 0.405
        , .names = "{.col}_ac"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_area_ha")
        , ~ .x * 2.471
        , .names = "{.col}_ac"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("kg_per_m2")
        , ~ .x * 0.20482
        , .names = "{.col}_lbsft2"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("kg_per_m3")
        , ~ .x * 0.0624
        , .names = "{.col}_lbsft3"
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        .cols = tidyselect::ends_with("_m2") & !tidyselect::ends_with("per_m2")
        , ~ .x * 10.764
        , .names = "{.col}_ft2"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename_with(
      .fn = function(x){dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_ends(x,"_cm_in") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_cm_in","_in")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_m_ft") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_m_ft","_ft")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_m2_per_ha_ftac") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_m2_per_ha_ftac","_ft2_per_ac")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_kg_per_ha_lbsac") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_kg_per_ha_lbsac","_lbs_per_ac")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_per_ha_ac") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_per_ha_ac","_per_ac")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_area_ha_ac") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_area_ha_ac","_area_ac")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_kg_per_m2_lbsft2") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_kg_per_m2_lbsft2","_lbs_per_ft2")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_kg_per_m3_lbsft3") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_kg_per_m3_lbsft3","_lbs_per_ft3")
        , stringr::str_ends(x,"_m2_ft2") ~ stringr::str_replace(x,"_m2_ft2","_ft2")
        , TRUE ~ x
      )}
    )
}

###################################################################################
### stand-level summaries
###################################################################################
calc_silv_metrics <- function(tree_list, stand_area_ha = NULL, study_boundary = NULL, calc_imperial_units = F) {
  # get study area
  if(!is.null(study_boundary)){
    # bounds check
    if(
      !inherits(study_boundary,"sf")
      && !inherits(study_boundary,"sfc")
    ){stop("study_boundary must be sf class object")}
    if(is.na(sf::st_crs(study_boundary))){stop("study_boundary does not have a CRS")}
    if(inherits(study_boundary,"sf") && nrow(study_boundary)!=1){
      stop("study_boundary must only have a single record geometry")
    }
    if(inherits(study_boundary,"sfc") && length(study_boundary)!=1){
      stop("study_boundary must only have a single record geometry")
    }
    if(
      !all( sf::st_is(study_boundary, c("POLYGON","MULTIPOLYGON")) )
    ){
      stop("study_boundary must contain POLYGON type geometry only")
    }
    # area
    xxstand_area_ha <- study_boundary %>% 
      sf::st_area() %>% 
      as.numeric() %>% 
      `/`(10000)
  }else if(is.numeric(stand_area_ha)){
    xxstand_area_ha <- stand_area_ha[1]
  }else{
    stop("must provide `stand_area_ha` as numeric or `study_boundary` as sf object")
  }
  
  if(is.null(xxstand_area_ha) || is.na(xxstand_area_ha) || dplyr::coalesce(xxstand_area_ha,0)<=0){
    stop("could not determine valid stand_area_ha")
  }
  
  # summarize tree list
  if(!inherits(tree_list,"data.frame")){stop("tree_list must be data.frame class object")}
  
  ###### !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! NEED TO PUT IN CHECKS FOR COLUMNS USED
  # see: cloud2trees::check_df_cols_all_missing()
  if( !any(stringr::str_detect(names(tree_list), "landfire_crown_biomass_kg")) ){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% dplyr::mutate(landfire_crown_biomass_kg=as.numeric(NA))
  }
  if( !any(stringr::str_detect(names(tree_list), "cruz_crown_biomass_kg")) ){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% dplyr::mutate(cruz_crown_biomass_kg=as.numeric(NA))
  }
  if( !any(stringr::str_detect(names(tree_list), "landfire_tree_kg_per_m3")) ){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% dplyr::mutate(landfire_tree_kg_per_m3=as.numeric(NA))
  }
  if( !any(stringr::str_detect(names(tree_list), "cruz_tree_kg_per_m3")) ){
    tree_list <- tree_list %>% dplyr::mutate(cruz_tree_kg_per_m3=as.numeric(NA))
  }
  
  # agg
  agg <- tree_list %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_trees = dplyr::n()
      , mean_dbh_cm = mean(dbh_cm, na.rm = T)
      , mean_tree_height_m = mean(tree_height_m, na.rm = T)
      , mean_tree_cbh_m = mean(tree_cbh_m, na.rm = T)
      , loreys_height_m = sum(basal_area_m2*tree_height_m, na.rm = T) / sum(basal_area_m2, na.rm = T)
      , basal_area_m2 = sum(basal_area_m2, na.rm = T)
      , sum_dbh_cm_sq = sum(dbh_cm^2, na.rm = T)
      , landfire_crown_biomass_kg = sum(landfire_crown_biomass_kg, na.rm = F)
      , cruz_crown_biomass_kg = sum(cruz_crown_biomass_kg, na.rm = F)
      , mean_landfire_tree_kg_per_m3 = mean(landfire_tree_kg_per_m3, na.rm = T)
      , mean_cruz_tree_kg_per_m3 = mean(cruz_tree_kg_per_m3, na.rm = T)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      stand_area_ha = xxstand_area_ha
      , trees_per_ha = (n_trees/stand_area_ha)
      , basal_area_m2_per_ha = (basal_area_m2/stand_area_ha)
      , qmd_cm = sqrt(sum_dbh_cm_sq/n_trees)
      , landfire_cfl_kg_per_m2 = landfire_crown_biomass_kg/(stand_area_ha*10000)
      , cruz_cfl_kg_per_m2 = cruz_crown_biomass_kg/(stand_area_ha*10000)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-c(sum_dbh_cm_sq,landfire_crown_biomass_kg,cruz_crown_biomass_kg))
  # imperial
  if(calc_imperial_units){
    agg <- calc_imperial_units_fn(agg)
  }
  return(agg)
}
```

check out the data structure returned by the `calc_silv_metrics()` function for a *single example treatment unit*

    tree_list = treetops_sf %>% 
      # just get one unit
      dplyr::filter(
        trtmnt_type==treetops_sf$trtmnt_type[1]
        , trtmnt_block==treetops_sf$trtmnt_block[1]
        , trtmnt_unit==treetops_sf$trtmnt_unit[1]
      )
    , stand_area_ha = treetops_sf$trtmnt_unit_area_ha[1]
    , calc_imperial_units = T
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::glimpse()
```

## Treatment Unit Summaries

let's summarize the tree data by treatment unit

```{r}
unit_sum_df <-
  treetops_sf %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::distinct(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit,trtmnt_unit_area_ha)
unit_sum_df <-
  1:nrow(unit_sum_df) %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    unit_temp <- unit_sum_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
    unit_temp %>% 
      dplyr::bind_cols(
        calc_silv_metrics(
          tree_list = treetops_sf %>% 
            # just get one unit
            dplyr::inner_join(
              unit_temp
              , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
            )
          , stand_area_ha = unit_temp$trtmnt_unit_area_ha
          , calc_imperial_units = T
        )
      )
  }) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    my_fct = forcats::fct_cross(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(desc(trtmnt_type),trees_per_ha) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(my_fct = forcats::fct_inorder(my_fct))

# reusable function for plotting
plt_metric_dist_fn <- function(df, metric_name, metric_label = NA) {
  if(any(is.na(metric_label))){metric_label <- metric_name}
  tit <- paste(
    "distribution of treatment unit"
    ,metric_label
  ) %>% 
  latex2exp::TeX()
  
  df %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(x=.data[[metric_name]],fill=trtmnt_type)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(mapping = ggplot2::aes(y=ggplot2::after_stat(scaled)), alpha = 0.8, color = NA) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    rows = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_type)
    , axes = "all"
    , switch = "y"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA),labels = scales::comma, breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n=6)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(NULL,breaks=NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    fill="",x=latex2exp::TeX(metric_label),y=""
    , title = tit
    , subtitle = "\nby treatment type"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)
    , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = -20, unit = "pt"))
    
  )
}
plt_metric_violin_fn <- function(df, metric_name, metric_label = NA) {
  if(any(is.na(metric_label))){metric_label <- metric_name}
  tit <- paste(
    "distribution of treatment unit"
    ,metric_label
  ) %>% 
  latex2exp::TeX()
  
  df %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(mapping = ggplot2::aes(x=.data[[metric_name]])) +
  ggplot2::geom_violin(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = 0, fill=trtmnt_type)
    , alpha = 0.8, color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, fill = NA, outliers = F) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    rows = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_type)
    , axes = "all"
    , switch = "y"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA),labels = scales::comma, breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n=6)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(NULL,breaks=NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    fill="",x=latex2exp::TeX(metric_label),y=""
    , title = tit
    , subtitle = "\nby treatment type"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)
    , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = -20, unit = "pt"))
  )
}

```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE, fig.height=8}
