```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE, fig.height=8}
  dplyr::select(trtmnt_type, tree_height_m, crown_diameter_m) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c(trtmnt_type)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    name = dplyr::recode_values(
      name
      , "tree_height_m" ~ "tree height (m)"
      , "dbh_cm" ~ "tree DBH (cm)"
      , "crown_area_m2" ~ "crown area (m²)"
      , "crown_diameter_m" ~ "crown diam. (m)"
    )
  ) %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = trtmnt_type)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = value,y=ggplot2::after_stat(scaled))
    , alpha = 0.8, color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    data = 
      treetops_sf %>%
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
        dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(
          .cols = c(tree_height_m,crown_diameter_m) 
          , ~median(.x,na.rm=T)
        )) %>% 
        tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -c(trtmnt_type)) %>% 
        dplyr::mutate(
          name = dplyr::recode_values(
            name
            , "tree_height_m" ~ "tree height (m)"
            , "dbh_cm" ~ "tree DBH (cm)"
            , "crown_area_m2" ~ "crown area (m²)"
            , "crown_diameter_m" ~ "crown diam. (m)"
          )
        )
    , mapping = ggplot2::aes(xintercept = value)
    , linetype = "dashed", lwd = 1, color = "gray33"
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    rows = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_type)
    , cols = dplyr::vars(name)
    # rows = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_block)
    , axes = "all"
    , switch = "y"
    , scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA),labels = scales::comma, breaks=scales::breaks_extended(n=10)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(NULL,breaks=NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    fill=""
    , x=""
    ,y=""
    , title = "distribution of individual tree measurements with line at median value"
    , subtitle = "\nby treatment type"
    , caption = "*minimum height to be considered a 'tree': 2 m"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)
    , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = -20, unit = "pt"))
  )
```

```{r, include = F, eval = F}
# make ggplot2::cut_* bins pretty
make_bins_pretty <- function(bin_factor, suffix = "") {
  # convert factor to character and remove brackets and parens
  clean_labels <- bin_factor %>%
    as.character() %>%
    stringr::str_replace_all(c("\\[" = "", "\\(" = "", "\\]" = "", "\\)" = "")) %>%
    stringr::str_replace(",", "-")
  
  # suffix
  if(stringr::str_squish(suffix) != "" && inherits(suffix,"character")){
    clean_labels <- stringr::str_c(clean_labels, " ", suffix) %>% stringr::str_squish()
  }
  
  # reorder based on the original factor levels 
  forcats::fct_reorder(factor(clean_labels), as.numeric(bin_factor))
}
```

```{r, include=F, eval=F}
      dplyr::summarise(trtmnt_unit_area_ha=sum(trtmnt_unit_area_ha,na.rm=T))
```

```{r}
  dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct = n/sum(n)
    , tph = n/trtmnt_unit_area_ha
    , lab = ifelse(
      pct>0.02
      , paste0(scales::comma(tph,accuracy=1), "\n",scales::percent(pct,accuracy=1) )
      , ""
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  
  ###### this makes sure the long tail isn't plotted :/

  dplyr::arrange(trtmnt_type,tree_height_m_bin) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cum = cumsum(pct)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tree_height_m_bin) %>%
  dplyr::filter(min(cum)<0.998) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  ###### this makes sure the long tail isn't plotted :/
```

```{r}
# unique units
unq_units_df <- treetops_sf %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%

# function to plot ortho
terra_plt_ortho <- function(
  ortho
  , crowns
  , boundary
  , title
  , add_crowns = T
) {
  if(terra::nlyr(ortho)==3){
    terra::plotRGB(
      ortho
      , stretch = "lin"
      # , mar = c(b,l,t,r)
      , mar = c(0.2,0.2,2.2,0.2)
      , plg = list(
        title.cex = 0.5
      )
      , main = title, cex.main=0.7
    ) 
  }else{
    terra::plot(
      ortho
      , col = viridis::plasma(n=100)
      # , mar = c(b,l,t,r)
      , mar = c(0.2,0.2,2.2,3.5)
      , axes = F
      , plg = list(
        # title = "CHM (m)"
        cex = 0.8, title.cex = 0.5, shrink = 0.6
      )
      , main = title, cex.main=0.7
    ) 
  }
  terra::plot(
    boundary %>% 
      sf::st_transform(terra::crs(ortho)) %>% 
      terra::vect()
    , add = T, border = "black", col = NA
  )
  if(add_crowns){
    terra::plot(
      crowns %>% 
        sf::st_transform(terra::crs(ortho)) %>% 
        terra::vect()
      , add = T
      , border = harrypotter::hp(n=2, option="hermionegranger")[2] # "cyan"
      , col = NA, lwd = 0.6
    )
  }
}
```

# Tree Group Analysis

Evaluate the spatial configuration of the detected trees focusing on horizontal heterogeneity and an investigation of tree clumps and openings.

some relevant work includes:

* *Spatial Patterns of Pinyon–Juniper Woodland Expansion in Central Nevada* ([Weisberg et al. 2007](https://doi.org/10.2111/05-224R2.1))
* *Density-dependent tree mortality in pinyon-juniper woodlands* ([Greenwood and Weisberg 2008](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foreco.2007.12.048))
* *Long-Term Effectiveness of Tree Removal to Re-Establish Sagebrush Steppe Vegetation and Associated Spatial Patterns in Surface Conditions and Soil Hydrologic Properties* ([Williams et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/w12082213))

## Group Tree Crowns

While some research on tree spatial patterns use tree point locations buffered with a fixed radius (e.g. 3 m) to approximate the crown radius of a "typical" overstory tree
(e.g. [Churchill et al. (2016)](https://scholarworks.umt.edu/ico/3)), we'll use the irregular, more realistic crown shapes identified from the aerial data to determine tree clump groups.

Remember we are only looking at what could be considered "overstory" trees since we filtered the tree list to keep only trees that meet a certain minimum height threshold of `r min_tree_ht_m` m

```{r, echo=T}
treetops_sf %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::select(tree_height_m) %>% 
  summary() %>% 
  knitr::kable(format = "markdown")
```

Since a primary objective of this analysis is to evaluate how [different treatments](#silv_sum) influence forest structure, we'll treat each unit as a discrete area and exclude any trees located outside of the unit boundaries from the clump classification process. This approach assumes that trees within a unit do not form functional clusters with those in adjacent areas (even though some units share a common border and we have data extending beyond the unit boundaries). This assumption prevents data from untreated control areas or differently treated areas from influencing the results when summarized by treatment type. This intentional ignorance of edge effects means that the scale of focus of this analysis is strictly on the treatment unit.

define a function to make the tree clump groupings by treatment unit

```{r, eval = F, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
c2t_output_dir <- "../data"
c2t_process_dir <- file.path(c2t_output_dir, "point_cloud_processing_delivery")

   dplyr::rename_with(~stringr::str_replace_all(.x, "\\.{2,}", ".")) %>%
```

```{r, results=F}
get_clumps_temp <- function(tree_list, buffer = 0) {
  # buffer and dissolve (arcGIS logic)
  clump_polys <- tree_list %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    sf::st_buffer(buffer) %>% 
    sf::st_union() %>%
    sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(clump_id = dplyr::row_number())

  # attach to trees
  trees_with_clumps <- tree_list %>%
    # get rid of columns we'll create
    dplyr::select( -dplyr::any_of(c(
      "hey_xxxxxxxxxx"
      , "clump_id"
      , "clump_n_trees"
      , "clump_n_trees_grp"
      , "clump_dist_m"
    ))) %>%
    sf::st_join(clump_polys %>% dplyr::select(clump_id), join = sf::st_intersects, largest = T) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(clump_id) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      clump_n_trees = dplyr::n()
      , clump_n_trees_grp = dplyr::case_when(
        clump_n_trees == 1 ~ "Individual"
        , clump_n_trees >= 2 & clump_n_trees <= 4 ~ "2-4 trees"
        
        , clump_n_trees >= 5 & clump_n_trees <= 10 ~ "5-10 trees"
        , clump_n_trees > 10 ~ ">10 trees"
        # , clump_n_trees >= 5 & clump_n_trees <= 9 ~ "5-9 trees"
        # , clump_n_trees >= 10 & clump_n_trees <= 15 ~ "10-15 trees"
        # , clump_n_trees > 15 ~ ">15 trees"
        # # , T ~ "error"
      ) %>%
      factor(
        ordered = T
        , levels = c("Individual", "2-4 trees", "5-10 trees", ">10 trees")
        # , levels = c("Individual", "2-4 trees", "5-9 trees", "10-15 trees", ">15 trees")
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  # add back to clumps
  clump_polys <- clump_polys %>% 
    dplyr::inner_join(
      trees_with_clumps %>% 
        sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
        dplyr::distinct(clump_id, clump_n_trees, clump_n_trees_grp)
      , by = "clump_id"
    )
  return(list(clump_polys = clump_polys, tree_list = trees_with_clumps))
}
# buffer for UAS-delineated crown polygons
my_buffer <- 1
```

make the clump groups using the UAS-delineated crown polygons. because we are using the irregular crown shapes that align with real-world crowns and want to account for slight misalignment between the UAS GPS and on-the-ground conditions we'll define clump group membership using a `r my_buffer/2` m buffer on the crowns. Under this condition, trees that do not have interlocking crowns based on UAS delineations but are within `r my_buffer` m of one another will be considered part of the same tree clump group. We'll use this same `r my_buffer` m distance threshold in defining treeless openings which will be required to comprise continuous space at least `r my_buffer` m away from the nearest tree.

```{r grp-them-crwns, results=F}
# crowns_sf %>% dplyr::glimpse()

  !file.exists(crowns_clump_fnm) ||
  !file.exists(clump_polys_fnm)
){
  get_clumps_ans_temp <- 
    1:nrow(unq_units_df) %>% 
    purrr::map(function(x, buff = my_buffer/2){
      crowns_sf %>% 
        dplyr::inner_join(
          unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
          , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
        ) %>% 
        get_clumps_temp(buffer = buff)
    })
  # get trees
  crowns_sf <-
    get_clumps_ans_temp %>%
    purrr::map(
      \(x) purrr::pluck(x,"tree_list")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::bind_rows()
  # get clump polygons
  clump_polys <-
    1:nrow(unq_units_df) %>% 
    purrr::map(
      \(x)
      get_clumps_ans_temp[[x]] %>% 
        purrr::pluck("clump_polys") %>% 
        sf::st_set_geometry("geometry") %>% 
        dplyr::bind_cols(
          unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
        )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::bind_rows()
  
  # write
  crowns_sf %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::select(treeID, tidyselect::starts_with("clump_")) %>% 
    readr::write_csv(file = crowns_clump_fnm, append = F, progress = F)
  
  clump_polys %>% 
    sf::st_write(dsn = clump_polys_fnm, append = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
}else{
  crowns_sf <- crowns_sf %>% 
    dplyr::select(-tidyselect::starts_with("clump_")) %>% 
    dplyr::inner_join(readr::read_csv(crowns_clump_fnm, progress = F), by = "treeID") %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      clump_n_trees_grp =  
        clump_n_trees_grp%>%
        factor(
          ordered = T
          , levels = c("Individual", "2-4 trees", "5-10 trees", ">10 trees")
          # , levels = c("Individual", "2-4 trees", "5-9 trees", "10-15 trees", ">15 trees")
        )
    )
  # clump_polys
  clump_polys <- sf::st_read(clump_polys_fnm, quiet = T) 
  clump_polys <- 
    clump_polys %>% 
    # convert to factors
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(
          names(clump_polys)[names(clump_polys) %in% names(unq_units_df)]
        )
        , ~ factor(
          .x
          , levels = levels(unq_units_df[[dplyr::cur_column()]])
          , ordered = T
        )
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(c("clump_n_trees_grp"))
        , ~ factor(
          .x
          , levels = levels(crowns_sf[[dplyr::cur_column()]])
          , ordered = T
        )
      ) 
    )
}

```

let's look at what this clump definition did

```{r, include=F, eval = T}
get_huge_palette <- function(n_colors) {
  # 1. Establish the universally trusted, high-contrast Okabe-Ito base anchors
  # These are optimized for Protan, Deutan, and Tritan colorblindness
  okabe_ito <- c(
    "#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#56B4E9", 
    "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#F0E442", "#000000"
  )
  
  # Calculate remaining slots needed
  rem_colors <- base::max(0, n_colors - base::length(okabe_ito))
  colors_per_tier <- base::ceiling(rem_colors / 3)
  
  # 2. Build 3 hyper-contrasting HCL bands with maximized saturation
  # Band 1: Midnight/Deep tones (Low luminance, high chroma)
  tier_dark <- grDevices::hcl(
    h = base::seq(from = 0, to = 330, length.out = colors_per_tier), 
    c = 85, 
    l = 25
  )
  
  # Band 2: Electric/Vibrant tones (Medium luminance, max chroma)
  tier_medium <- grDevices::hcl(
    h = base::seq(from = 40, to = 370, length.out = colors_per_tier), 
    c = 95, 
    l = 55
  )
  
  # Band 3: Neon Pastel/Light tones (High luminance, moderate chroma)
  tier_light <- grDevices::hcl(
    h = base::seq(from = 20, to = 350, length.out = colors_per_tier), 
    c = 65, 
    l = 85
  )
  
  # 3. Interleave the three bands using tidyverse to enforce severe brightness jumps
  generated_colors <- tibble::tibble(
    dark   = tier_dark,
    medium = tier_medium,
    light  = tier_light
  ) %>%  
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::everything(), 
      names_to = "tier", 
      values_to = "hex_color"
    ) %>%  
    dplyr::mutate(nr = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
    # dplyr::slice_sample(n=n_colors*2) %>% 
    dplyr::slice_head(n=n_colors) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(nr) %>% 
    dplyr::pull(hex_color)
  
  # Combine anchors with generated colors
  raw_palette <- base::c(okabe_ito, generated_colors)[1:n_colors]
  
  # 4. Apply a wide mathematical dispersion stride
  # This breaks up the sequential sweeps entirely, packing contrasting tones side-by-side
  stride <- base::ceiling(base::sqrt(n_colors))
  indices <- base::seq(from = 1, to = n_colors, by = 1)
  dispersed_indices <- base::order((indices - 1) %% stride, (indices - 1) %/% stride)
  
  final_palette <- raw_palette[dispersed_indices]
  
  return(final_palette)
}
```

## Identify Openings

Let's identify the gaps within a treatment unit. We'll identify openings based on their distance from the nearest tree crown. We'll use this same `r my_buffer` m distance threshold in defining treeless openings, where each opening will be required to comprise continuous space at least `r my_buffer` m away from the nearest tree. This `r my_buffer` m buffer accounts for the zone of immediate canopy influence and ensures that areas categorized as open are functionally distinct from the canopy. This threshold is flexible and can be adjusted to meet specific management or analysis objectives (e.g. flame length; wildlife corridors). 

First, we'll generate a distance raster where each cell represents the distance to the nearest tree clump group (i.e. crown) within the treatment unit boundary. Areas with a distance value of `r my_buffer` m or greater are classified as openings and are defined by spatial connectedness, not a specific geometric shape. As such, they may be irregularly shaped as they are allowed to wind between clumps to follow a path where trees are distant. A single opening continues as long as the flow of open space is not entirely obstructed by surrounding tree groups. Once a gap is completely surrounded by canopy, the opening is closed off and is treated as a discrete spatial feature.

```{r}
# create function to pass a return from get_clump_summary() and get a distance raster
get_clump_dist_rast_temp <- function(x, clump_dist_m = 3){
  # get clump_dist_m
  # clump_dist_m <- min(get_clump_summary_ans$clump_dist_m, na.rm = T)
  # rasterize the clump polygons and then calculate distance between clumps as raster
  dist_rast <-
    terra::rasterize(
        x = 
          crowns_sf %>% 
          dplyr::inner_join(
            unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
            , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
          ) %>% 
          terra::vect()
        , y = 
          # crowns_sf %>% 
          # dplyr::inner_join(
          #   unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
          #   , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
          # ) %>% 
          # terra::vect() %>%
          stand_boundary %>% 
          dplyr::filter(
            unit == unq_units_df$trtmnt_unit[x]
            , block == unq_units_df$trtmnt_block[x]
            , stringr::str_squish(tolower(tretmnt)) == unq_units_df$trtmnt_type[x]
          ) %>% 
          terra::vect() %>% 
          terra::rast(res = 0.2)
      ) %>% 
      terra::distance() %>% 
      # crop it to stand extent
      terra::crop(
        stand_boundary %>% 
          dplyr::filter(
            unit == unq_units_df$trtmnt_unit[x]
            , block == unq_units_df$trtmnt_block[x]
            , stringr::str_squish(tolower(tretmnt)) == unq_units_df$trtmnt_type[x]
          ) %>% 
          terra::vect()
        , mask = T
      )
  ######### part 2
  # now create openings vector data
  openings_vect <- 
    dist_rast %>% 
      terra::classify(rcl = c(clump_dist_m,Inf), others = NA, include.lowest = T) %>% 
      terra::as.polygons(na.rm = T) %>% 
      sf::st_as_sf() %>% 
      sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(layer = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        openining_area_m2 = sf::st_area(geometry) %>% as.numeric()
        , clump_dist_m = clump_dist_m
      )
  
  # return
  return(list(dist_rast = dist_rast, openings_vect = openings_vect))
}
```

```{r}
get_clump_dist_rast_ans <-

    get_clump_dist_rast_temp(

    )
  )
```

```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE, results=F, fig.show='asis', fig.height=9.5, fig.width=9.5}
# mapping
plt_blk_temp <- function(blk, add = F, save = F) {
  # which idx
  idx_temp <- 
    unq_units_df %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(rownum = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(trtmnt_block==blk) %>% 
    dplyr::pull(rownum)
  # max dist
  max_d <- 
    purrr::map(get_clump_dist_rast_ans[idx_temp], "dist_rast") %>% 
    purrr::map(
      \(r)
      terra::minmax(r) %>% 
        .[2] %>% 
        ceiling()  
    ) %>% 
    purrr::compact() %>% 
    unlist() %>% 
    max(na.rm = T)
  # plts
  plts_temp <- 
    idx_temp %>% 
    purrr::map(\(x) plt_dist_rast_fn(x, add_clumps = add, max_dist = max_d))
  # patchwork
  p_temp <- 
    patchwork::wrap_plots(
      plts_temp
      , ncol = 2
      , guides = "collect"
    ) &
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # save 
  if(save){
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = file.path("../data", paste0("plt_dist_block_", blk, ".png"))
      , plot = p_temp
      , width = 10
      , height = 10
      , dpi = 300
    )
  }else{
    p_temp
  }
}
```

```{r, results=F, fig.show='asis'}
plt_openings_vect_fn <- 
  function(x, add_clumps = F, max_area = NA){
    plt_tit <- paste0(
      unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x) %>% dplyr::pull(trtmnt_type)
      , " | block "
      , unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x) %>% dplyr::pull(trtmnt_block)
      , " | "
      , unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x) %>% dplyr::pull(trtmnt_unit)
    )
    
    # get around empty levels that causes problems in the legend of ggplot
    blank_df <- 
      dplyr::tibble(
        clump_n_trees_grp = levels(clump_polys$clump_n_trees_grp) %>% 
          ordered(levels = levels(clump_polys$clump_n_trees_grp))
        , geometry = rep("GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY", length(levels(clump_polys$clump_n_trees_grp))) %>% 
          sf::st_as_sfc(crs = sf::st_crs(clump_polys))
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_as_sf()

    
    # plt unit
    unit_temp <- stand_boundary %>% 
      dplyr::filter(
        unit == unq_units_df$trtmnt_unit[x]
        , block == unq_units_df$trtmnt_block[x]
        , stringr::str_squish(tolower(tretmnt)) == unq_units_df$trtmnt_type[x]
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(terra::crs(chm_rast))
    
    plt_stand <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::geom_sf(data = unit_temp, color = "black", fill = NA) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = ""
        , y = ""
        , subtitle = plt_tit
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_void() +
      ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "top" # c(0.5,1)
        , legend.direction = "horizontal"
        , legend.box = "vertical"
        , legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(2.5,0,0,0) # trbl
        , legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7)
        , legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6)
        , legend.key = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA)
        , legend.key.size = unit(0.5, "cm")
        # , plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 10, hjust = 0.5)
        , plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
        , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
      )
    # add open
    plt_open <- 
      plt_stand +
      # openings
      ggplot2::geom_sf(
        data = get_clump_dist_rast_ans[[x]][["openings_vect"]]
        , mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = openining_area_m2), color = NA
      )
      # ggplot2::guides(
      #   fill = ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
      #     label.theme = ggplot2::element_text(
      #       angle = 45, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.4, size = 8
      #     )
      #   )
      # )
      
    if(!is.na(max_area)){
      plt_open <- plt_open +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
          low = "gray77", high = "gray11"
          , labels = scales::comma_format(accuracy = 1)
          , name = "opening\narea (m²)" #latex2exp::TeX("opening\narea ($\\m^2$)")
          , limits = c(0,max_area)
          , guide = ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
            label.theme = ggplot2::element_text(
              angle = 55
              , hjust = 1
              , vjust = 1.3
            )
          )
        )
    }else{
      plt_open <- plt_open +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
          low = "gray77", high = "gray11"
          , labels = scales::comma_format(accuracy = 1)
          , name = "opening\narea (m²)" #latex2exp::TeX("opening\narea ($\\m^2$)")
          # , limits = c(0,max_area)
          , guide = ggplot2::guide_colorbar(
            label.theme = ggplot2::element_text(
              angle = 55
              , hjust = 1
              , vjust = 1.3
            )
          )
        )
    }
    # add clumps
    if(add_clumps){
      plt_open <- plt_open +
        # clumps
        ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
        ggplot2::geom_sf(
          data = clump_polys %>% 
            dplyr::inner_join(
              unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
              , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
            ) %>% 
            dplyr::select(clump_n_trees_grp)
          # , mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = clump_n_trees_grp)
          , color = "gray33"
          , fill = NA
        ) +
        ggplot2::geom_sf(
          data = crowns_sf %>% 
            dplyr::inner_join(
              unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
              , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
            ) %>% 
            dplyr::select(clump_n_trees_grp) %>% 
            dplyr::bind_rows(blank_df)
          , mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = clump_n_trees_grp)
          , color = NA
        ) +
        # harrypotter::scale_fill_hp_d("always", name = "clump size", drop = F) +
        ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = hey_clump_pal, name = "", drop = F, limits = levels(crowns_sf$clump_n_trees_grp)) +
        # tree points
        ggplot2::geom_sf(
          data = 
            treetops_sf %>% 
            dplyr::inner_join(
              unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
              , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
            )
          , color = "gray88", shape = "."
        )
        # ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 2))
    }
    return(plt_open)
  }
# one unit
```

```{r,eval=T,purl=FALSE, results=F, fig.show='asis', fig.height=9.5, fig.width=9.5}
# mapping
plt_blk_temp <- function(blk, add = F, save = F) {
  # which idx
  idx_temp <- 
    unq_units_df %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(rownum = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(trtmnt_block==blk) %>% 
    dplyr::pull(rownum)
  # max dist
  max_d <-
    purrr::map(get_clump_dist_rast_ans[idx_temp], "openings_vect") %>%
    dplyr::bind_rows() %>% 
    dplyr::pull(openining_area_m2) %>% 
    max(na.rm = T) %>% 
    ceiling()
  # plts
  plts_temp <- 
    idx_temp %>% 
    purrr::map(\(x) plt_openings_vect_fn(x, add_clumps = add, max_area = max_d))
  # patchwork
  p_temp <- 
    patchwork::wrap_plots(
      plts_temp
      , ncol = 2
      , guides = "collect"
    ) &
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # save 
  if(save){
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      filename = file.path("../data", paste0("plt_open_block_", blk, ".png"))
      , plot = p_temp
      , width = 10
      , height = 10
      , dpi = 300
    )
  }else{
    p_temp
  }
}
```

## Tree Clump Summary

let's get some summary stats of the tree clump groupings by treatment type

```{r}
# create a function to summarize by number of tree clump grouping
get_clump_n_trees_grp_summary_temp = function(x){
  # get area of harvest unit
  #...will use this area in the area calculations such that...
  #...TPA = trees in a certain group size across the whole stand area
  harvest_area_ha <- 
    stand_boundary %>% 
    dplyr::filter(
      unit == unq_units_df$trtmnt_unit[x]
      , block == unq_units_df$trtmnt_block[x]
      , stringr::str_squish(tolower(tretmnt)) == unq_units_df$trtmnt_type[x]
    ) %>% 
    sf::st_transform(terra::crs(chm_rast)) %>% 
    sf::st_union() %>% 
    sf::st_as_sf() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(harvest_area_ha = sf::st_area(.) %>% as.numeric() %>% `/`(10000)) %>% 
    dplyr::pull(harvest_area_ha) %>% 
    .[1]
  # which dta
  get_tree_clumps_ans <- 
    crowns_sf %>% 
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::inner_join(
      unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)
      , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(stand_area_ha = harvest_area_ha)
  # collapse and calculate silv metrics
  dta <- 
    get_tree_clumps_ans %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit,stand_area_ha,clump_n_trees_grp) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      # summary metrics
      n_trees = dplyr::n_distinct(treeID)
      , mean_dbh_cm = mean(dbh_cm, na.rm = T)
      , mean_tree_height_m = mean(tree_height_m, na.rm = T)
      , mean_crown_diameter_m = mean(crown_diameter_m, na.rm = T)
      # , loreys_height_m = sum(basal_area_m2*tree_height_m, na.rm = T) / sum(basal_area_m2, na.rm = T)
      # , basal_area_m2 = sum(basal_area_m2, na.rm = T)
      # , sum_dbh_cm_sq = sum(dbh_cm^2, na.rm = T)
      , .groups = "drop_last"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      trees_per_ha = (n_trees/stand_area_ha) # (n_trees/clump_area_ha) ... this was not right
      # , basal_area_m2_per_ha = (basal_area_m2/stand_area_ha) # (basal_area_m2/clump_area_ha) ... this was not right
      # , qmd_cm = sqrt(sum_dbh_cm_sq/n_trees)
      # stand calcs
      , stand_trees_per_ha = sum(n_trees)/stand_area_ha
      # , stand_basal_area_m2 = sum(basal_area_m2)
      # , stand_basal_area_m2_per_ha = sum(basal_area_m2)/stand_area_ha
      # , pct_stand_basal_area = basal_area_m2/stand_basal_area_m2
      , pct_stand_n_trees = n_trees/sum(n_trees)
      # , stand_qmd_cm = sqrt(sum(get_tree_clumps_ans$dbh_cm^2, na.rm = T)/sum(n_trees))
    ) %>%
    # dplyr::select(-c(sum_dbh_cm_sq)) %>% 
    # convert to imperial units
    calc_imperial_units_fn()
  # fill in missing
  ret_dta <- 
    dplyr::tibble(
      # get all possible labels from the factor levels
      clump_n_trees_grp = levels(crowns_sf$clump_n_trees_grp)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(c("clump_n_trees_grp"))
        , ~ factor(
          .x
          , levels = levels(crowns_sf[[dplyr::cur_column()]])
          , ordered = T
        )
      )
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::bind_cols(unq_units_df %>% dplyr::slice(x)) %>% 
    dplyr::left_join(
      dta
      , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit,clump_n_trees_grp)
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        tidyselect::starts_with("stand_")
        , ~ max(.x, na.rm = T)
      )
      , dplyr::across(
        dplyr::where(is.numeric)
        , ~ dplyr::coalesce(.x, 0)
      )
    )
  # return
  return(ret_dta)
}
```

let's summarize the data by treatment type and plot it for those that prefer visualizations

```{r}
clump_n_trees_grp_summary %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type, clump_n_trees_grp) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(n = sum(n_trees)) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  # area by type
  dplyr::inner_join(
    unit_sum_df %>% 
      dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type) %>% 
      dplyr::summarise(trtmnt_unit_area_ha=sum(trtmnt_unit_area_ha,na.rm=T), .groups = "drop_last")
    , by = "trtmnt_type"
  ) %>% 
  calc_imperial_units_fn() %>% # get acres
  dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct = n/sum(n)
    # , pct_lab = scales::percent(pct,accuracy=0.1)
    , tpa = n/trtmnt_unit_area_ac
    , tph = n/trtmnt_unit_area_ha
    , lab = paste0(scales::comma(tph,accuracy=1), "\n",scales::percent(pct,accuracy=1) )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  # dplyr::glimpse()
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = tph, x = clump_n_trees_grp)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(fill = trtmnt_type)
    , width = 0.6
    , color = NA, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(label = lab)
    , color = "black", size = 2.5, vjust = -0.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(drop = F) + 
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    # breaks = seq(0,1,by=0.2)
    labels = scales::comma
    , expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0,0.1))
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    cols = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_type)
    # , rows = dplyr::vars(trtmnt_block)
    # , ncol = 2
    , axes = "all"
    # , switch = "y"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "tree clump size", y = "trees ha⁻¹", fill = ""
    , subtitle = "Trees per hectare by tree clump size"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
    # , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12)
    # , axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
    # , axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
clump_n_trees_grp_summary %>%
```

```{r}
  dplyr::summarise(n = sum(n_trees)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct = n/sum(n)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::select(trtmnt_type, clump_n_trees_grp, pct) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_lab = scales::percent(ifelse(pct>=0.08,pct,NA), accuracy = 1)
    , trtmnt_type = forcats::fct_rev(trtmnt_type)
    , clump_n_trees_grp = forcats::fct_rev(clump_n_trees_grp)
    , huh = ifelse(
      clump_n_trees_grp %in% c(">10 trees","5-10 trees")
      , "white"
      , "black"
    )
  ) %>% 
ggplot2::ggplot(
  mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = pct, y = trtmnt_type, fill=clump_n_trees_grp, group=clump_n_trees_grp)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    width = 0.7, alpha=0.95
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    mapping = aes(
        label = pct_lab
        , color = huh
        , fontface = "bold"
      )
    , position = ggplot2::position_stack(vjust = 0.5)
    # , color = "black"
    , size = 4
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = hey_clump_pal) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_identity() +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    fill = "clump\nsize"
    , y = ""
    , x = "proportion of trees in different sized clumps"
    , subtitle = "Study-wide tree proportions by tree clump size"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "top"
    , legend.direction  = "horizontal"
    , legend.title = element_text(size=7)
    , axis.title.x = element_text(size=10, face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = element_blank()
    , axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
    , axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      # nrow = 2, byrow = T, 
      reverse = T
      # , override.aes = list(alpha = 0.9)
    )
  )
```

## Openings Summary

lastly, we'll look at the openings information. 

we define openings as contiguous spatial areas that originate `r my_buffer` m away from the nearest tree crown. Although these openings may form highly sinuous (“wavy”) corridors winding through tree clump groups, they are closed-off wherever the flow of open space is entirely obstructed by surrounding tree groups. Once a gap is completely surrounded by canopy, the opening is closed off and is treated as a discrete spatial feature. We also require that an opening must have an area greater than 40.5 square meters (0.01 acres) to be considered an actual opening.

```{r}
my_min_openining_area_m2 <- 0.01*4047 # 1/100 of an acre where 4047=sq m in 1 acre

open_full_temp <- 
  get_clump_dist_rast_ans %>% 
  purrr::map(purrr::pluck("openings_vect")) %>%
  purrr::list_rbind(names_to = "row_num") %>% 
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(unq_units_df %>% dplyr::mutate(row_num = dplyr::row_number()), by = "row_num") %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    openining_area_m2 > my_min_openining_area_m2
  )
# dplyr::glimpse(open_full_temp)
# stand_boundary %>% nrow()
# stand_boundary %>% names()
# unit_sum_df %>% dplyr::glimpse()
cc_df_temp <- 
  1:nrow(unit_sum_df) %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    # crown area
    area_m2_temp <- 
      crowns_sf %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::select(treeID) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(stand_boundary)) %>% 
      # crop crowns to treatment units
      sf::st_intersection(
        stand_boundary %>%
          dplyr::select(unit,block,tretmnt) %>% 
          dplyr::rename(type = tretmnt) %>% 
          dplyr::mutate(
            type =
              tolower(type) %>% 
              stringr::str_squish()
          ) %>% 
          dplyr::rename_with(.fn = ~paste0("trtmnt_", .x, recycle0 = T)) %>% 
          dplyr::inner_join(
            unit_sum_df %>% dplyr::slice(x) %>% 
              dplyr::select(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
            , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
          )
      ) %>% 
      # union by unit to dissolve internal boundaries
      sf::st_union() %>%
      sf::st_area() %>% 
      as.numeric()
    
    ret_df <- 
      unit_sum_df %>% 
      dplyr::slice(x) %>% 
      dplyr::select(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit,trtmnt_unit_area_ha) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        canopy_cov_area_m2 = dplyr::coalesce(area_m2_temp,0)
        , canopy_cov_area_ha = (canopy_cov_area_m2/10000)
        , canopy_cov_pct = canopy_cov_area_ha/trtmnt_unit_area_ha
      )
    return(ret_df)
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
# cc_df_temp %>% dplyr::glimpse()

# sum qualified openinings
open_temp <- 
  open_full_temp %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_openining_area_m2 = mean(openining_area_m2, na.rm = T)
    , median_openining_area_m2 = median(openining_area_m2, na.rm = T)
    , sum_openining_area_m2 = sum(openining_area_m2, na.rm = T)
    , .groups = "drop_last"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    unit_sum_df %>% 
      dplyr::select(trtmnt_unit_area_ha,trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
    , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    sum_openining_area_ha = sum_openining_area_m2/10000
    , pct_open = sum_openining_area_ha/trtmnt_unit_area_ha
  ) %>% 
  # get canopy cover as well
  dplyr::left_join(
    cc_df_temp %>% dplyr::select(-c(trtmnt_unit_area_ha))
    , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
  )
  
# dplyr::glimpse(open_temp)
```

## Treatment Compliance Evaluation

The spatially-explicit forest inventories generated with UAS data and individual tree detection point cloud processing workflows enable evaluation of silvicultral treatment prescription compliance. For this specific project, the "uniform" thinning treatments provided explicit instructions for the spatial arrangement of post-treatment stand conditions:

***Uniform - Low***

>Light intensity thinning: Leave 15 feet between tree crowns. 70% of the retained (i.e. leave) trees should be over 8 inches basal diameter if present and 30% should be between 2 inches and 8 inches in basal diameter.

***Uniform - High***

>Heavy intensity thinning: Leave at least 30 feet between tree crowns; 70% of the retained (i.e. leave) trees should be over 8 inches basal diameter if present and 30% should be between 2 inches and 8 inches in basal diameter.

The following is a subset of items provided in the general guidance for both "uniform" prescriptions that are most relevant for our evaluation:

>d. Cut all dead pinyon trees <8 inches in basal diameter. Leave all other standing dead trees for wildlife snags. Dead trees are not considered when applying the spacing guides above.
>e. Remove 70% of all woody shrubs (i.e. gambel oak and serviceberry); retain all gambel oak stems greater than 3 inches in basal diameter. 
>f. All trees with green spray paint should be not be cut and piles should be placed at least 15 ft from the canopy of those trees. These have a small piece of equipment that are recording tree growth (Fig. 2). These point dendrometers are on the bole (main stem) of the tree, located 1-2 feet above the ground on the east side of the tree, and a shapefile of the trees approximate location has been provided.
>g. In addition to the above, the following apply:
  ....
  4.  Except for leave trees, all live trees having a minimum size of one (1) inch basal diameter and a height of 12 inches shall be cut. 
  5. Retain trees that contain raptor nests.
  6. No ponderosa pine trees should be cut

Since we know our UAS-based individual tree delineation [does not perfectly align with field-marked trees](#detect_acc_res) (`r scales::percent(agg_ground_truth_match_ans$f_score,accuracy=1)` F-score), we'll combine UAS-delineated tree crowns that are spatially continuous (i.e. directly touching or overlapping) into singular "tree objects" for this evaluation of the treatment tree spacing compliance. We'll then calculate the distance between spatially distinct post treatment tree objects for comparison against the prescription targets. Additionally, since the prescription requires that priority trees like ponderosa pine and wildlife trees are not removed, and thus excluded from the spacing guidelines, the average space between residual trees should be slightly lower than the targets (even if the spacing is perfectly implemented to prescription) due to these restrictions which require keeping more trees than would be needed to meet the spacing guidelines.

As a reminder, we are only evaluating UAS-detected tree objects that have a minimum height of `r min_tree_ht_m` m and have a top point that falls within a treatment unit boundary. This approach assumes that trees within a unit do not form functional clusters with those in adjacent areas (even though some units share a common border and we have data extending beyond the unit boundaries). This assumption prevents data from untreated control areas or differently treated areas from influencing the results when summarized by treatment type. This intentional ignorance of edge effects means that the scale of focus of this analysis is strictly on the treatment unit. As such, we'll limit the analysis to only portions of crowns that fall within the treatment unit boundary (excluding crown portions that are outside of the unit boundary).

```{r dist-my-resid-trees, results=F}
# combine trees crowns by unit to form tree object polygons
tree_obj_polys <- 
  1:nrow(unit_sum_df) %>% 
  purrr::map(function(x){
    unt_temp <- unit_sum_df %>% dplyr::slice(x) %>% 
      dplyr::select(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit,trtmnt_unit_area_ha)
    
    stand_temp <- 
      stand_boundary %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        unit==unt_temp$trtmnt_unit
        , block==unt_temp$trtmnt_block
        , tolower(stringr::str_squish(tretmnt))==unt_temp$trtmnt_type
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_transform(sf::st_crs(crowns_sf)) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(xxx=1) %>% 
      dplyr::select(xxx)
    
    tree_obj_polys_temp <- 
      crowns_sf %>% 
      dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
      dplyr::inner_join(
        unt_temp %>% dplyr::select(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
        , by = dplyr::join_by(trtmnt_type,trtmnt_block,trtmnt_unit)
      ) %>% 
      sf::st_intersection(stand_temp) %>% 
      dplyr::select(-xxx) %>% 
      sf::st_union() %>%
      sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
      sf::st_as_sf() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(tree_obj_id = dplyr::row_number()) %>% 
      dplyr::bind_cols(unt_temp) %>% 
      dplyr::relocate(tidyselect::starts_with("trtmnt_"))
    
    # for each tree obj (row) find the nearest other tree obj (non-self)
    # nearest_df_temp <-
    #   1:nrow(tree_obj_polys_temp) %>% 
    #   purrr::map(function(row_id){
    #     # curr
    #     current_geom <- sf::st_geometry(tree_obj_polys_temp)[row_id]
    #     # others
    #     other_geoms <- sf::st_geometry(tree_obj_polys_temp)[-row_id]
    #     # nearest
    #     n_idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(current_geom, other_geoms)
    #     # updt since we dropped this row_id from others
    #     n_idx <- ifelse(n_idx >= row_id, n_idx + 1, n_idx)
    #     # dist
    #     nearest_dist <- sf::st_distance(
    #       current_geom 
    #       , sf::st_geometry(tree_obj_polys_temp)[n_idx]
    #       , by_element = TRUE
    #     )
    #     # df
    #     df_ret <- dplyr::tibble(
    #       tree_obj_id = tree_obj_polys_temp$tree_obj_id[row_id]
    #       , nearest_tree_obj_id = tree_obj_polys_temp$tree_obj_id[n_idx]
    #       , nearest_dist_m = as.numeric(nearest_dist[1])
    #     )
    #     return(df_ret)
    #   }) %>% 
    #   purrr::list_rbind()
    
    # dist
    dm_temp <- sf::st_distance(tree_obj_polys_temp)
    # dm_temp
    # self-dist to Inf ... and beyond!!
    diag(dm_temp) <- Inf
    # for each row, get min dist (max -dist)
    nearest_idx_temp <- max.col(-dm_temp, ties.method = "first")
    # make it a matrix for filtering the distance matrix
    nearest_matrix_temp <- cbind(1:nrow(dm_temp), nearest_idx_temp)
    # filter dist matrix for just min dist by row
    dist_temp <- dm_temp[nearest_matrix_temp]
    
    # add it to the df
    # return
    ret_df <- 
      tree_obj_polys_temp %>% 
      # dplyr::left_join(nearest_df_temp, by = "tree_obj_id")
      
      dplyr::mutate(
        # nearest
        nearest_tree_obj_id = tree_obj_polys_temp$tree_obj_id[nearest_idx_temp]
        # dist
        , nearest_dist_m = as.numeric(dist_temp)
      )
    
    return(ret_df)
  }) %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind()
# add distance target
tree_obj_polys <-
  tree_obj_polys %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(
   unq_units_df %>% 
      dplyr::filter(
        stringr::str_starts(trtmnt_type, "uniform")
      ) %>% 
      dplyr::distinct(trtmnt_type) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(
        target_nearest_dist_m = dplyr::case_when(
          stringr::str_ends(trtmnt_type, "low") ~ 15/3.281
          , stringr::str_ends(trtmnt_type, "high") ~ 30/3.281
        )
      ) 
   , by = "trtmnt_type"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    target_nearest_dist_m = dplyr::coalesce(target_nearest_dist_m,-Inf)
    , is_within_presc_dist = ifelse(nearest_dist_m>=target_nearest_dist_m, "meets prescription", "fails prescription") %>% factor()
  )
  # sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% dplyr::count(trtmnt_type,is_within_presc_dist)
# huh?
tree_obj_polys %>% dplyr::glimpse()
```

```{r, include = F, eval = F}
plt_grid_fn_temp <- function(plot_list, ncol = 2, line_color = "lightgray", line_thickness = 0.02) {
  
  # 1. Define theme adjustments to apply to all subplots to shrink the legend space
  compact_theme <- ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
    , legend.key.size = ggplot2::unit(0.3, "cm")
    , legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 4.7)
    , legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 5)
    , legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
    , legend.box.spacing = ggplot2::unit(0.05, "cm")
    
    # , plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 10, hjust = 0.5)
    , plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")
    , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 5.5, hjust = 0.5)
    # , plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7)
  )
  
  # Apply the compact legend theme to every incoming plot
  plot_list <- lapply(plot_list, function(p) p + compact_theme)
  
  num_plots <- length(plot_list)
  num_rows <- ceiling(num_plots / ncol)
  
  # 2. Build the visual assets for the grid lines
  # Horizontal divider line asset
  hr_line <- patchwork::plot_spacer() + 
    ggplot2::theme(plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = line_color, color = NA))
  
  # Vertical divider line asset
  vr_line <- patchwork::plot_spacer() + 
    ggplot2::theme(plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = line_color, color = NA))
  
  # 3. Process the rows
  row_list <- list()
  row_heights <- c()
  
  for (i in 1:num_rows) {
    # Extract the subset of plots belonging to the current row
    start_idx <- ((i - 1) * ncol) + 1
    end_idx <- min(i * ncol, num_plots)
    row_subset <- plot_list[start_idx:end_idx]
    
    # If the last row is incomplete, pad it with blank spacers so alignment doesn't break
    if (length(row_subset) < ncol) {
      missing_slots <- ncol - length(row_subset)
      for (m in 1:missing_slots) {
        row_subset[[length(row_subset) + 1]] <- patchwork::plot_spacer()
      }
    }
    
    # Interleave vertical dividing lines between the plots in this row
    row_elements <- list()
    col_widths <- c()
    
    for (j in 1:length(row_subset)) {
      row_elements[[length(row_elements) + 1]] <- row_subset[[j]]
      col_widths <- c(col_widths, 1) # Width weight for the plot
      
      # Add a vertical divider if it's not the last plot in the row
      if (j < length(row_subset)) {
        row_elements[[length(row_elements) + 1]] <- vr_line
        col_widths <- c(col_widths, line_thickness) # Width weight for the vertical line
      }
    }
    
    # Assemble the final row layout
    completed_row <- patchwork::wrap_plots(row_elements, nrow = 1) + 
      patchwork::plot_layout(widths = col_widths)
    
    row_list[[length(row_list) + 1]] <- completed_row
    row_heights <- c(row_heights, 1) # Height weight for the row
    
    # Append a horizontal divider line if it's not the last row
    if (i < num_rows) {
      row_list[[length(row_list) + 1]] <- hr_line
      row_heights <- c(row_heights, line_thickness) # Height weight for the horizontal line
    }
  }
  
  # 4. Bind all constructed rows together vertically
  final_grid <- patchwork::wrap_plots(row_list, ncol = 1) + 
    patchwork::plot_layout(heights = row_heights)
  
  # 5. Automatically render/print the plot on execution
  print(final_grid)
  
  # Return the object invisibly so it can still be saved to a variable if needed
  return(invisible(final_grid))
}
```

```{r}
    , scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA),labels = scales::comma, breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n=6)) +
  # ggplot2::scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(NULL,breaks=NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    fill="",x="distance to\nnearest tree (m)",y=""
    , title = "distribution of post-treatment tree spacing distance to nearest neighbor"
    , subtitle = "\nby treatment type"
    , caption = "*note, independent x-axis range for each treatment type"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "none"
    , strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "black", face = "bold")
    , axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)
    , plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(t = -20, unit = "pt"))
  )
```

### Statistical Assessment of Post-Treatment Tree Spacing

let's evaluate how the different treatments influenced the spatial distribution of remaining trees by analyzing their nearest-neighbor distances.

#### Global Evaluation of Treatment Effects

We'll first use a global analysis of variance (ANOVA) style evaluation using joint tests to determine whether tree spacing differs significantly across any of the treatment types after controlling for treatment unit size since treatment unit size influences the maximum spacing of residual trees. A significant global result indicates that tree spacing changes with treatment type.

```{r}
library(lme4) # linear mixed-effects models
# ?lme4::lmer()
lm_nn <- lme4::lmer(
  nearest_dist_m ~ trtmnt_type + trtmnt_unit_area_ha + (1 | trtmnt_block) 
  , data = tree_obj_polys
)
# summary(lm_nn)
```

here are the global results which indicate whether treatment type significantly influenced tree spacing after accounting for treatment unit size

```{r, results='asis', warning=F}
# Compute joint tests of the terms in a model
# ?emmeans::joint_tests
joint_tests_temp <- emmeans::joint_tests(lm_nn)
joint_tests_temp %>% knitr::kable(format = "markdown")
```

the p-value for treatment type of `r scales::comma(joint_tests_temp$p.value[which(joint_tests_temp$`model term` %in% c("trtmnt_type"))], accuracy=0.0001)` indicates that the nearest-neighbor spacing `r ifelse(joint_tests_temp$p.value[which(joint_tests_temp$`model term` %in% c("trtmnt_type"))]<0.05,"differs", "does not differ")` significantly across the treatments after accounting for block variations and unit size

### Pairwise Treatment Comparisons

To identify which treatment(s) created unique tree spacing outcomes, we'll perform post-hoc pairwise contrasts among the different treatment groups. This comparison calculates the block-adjusted difference in average nearest-neighbor distances between every possible pair of treatments while keeping unit size constant at the mean.

let's get a summary table of the pairwise differences in average nearest-neighbor distances across treatment type

```{r}
# calculate estimated marginal means (emms) for each treatment
# holds trtmnt_unit_area_ha constant at its mean value and averages over the trtmnt_block
emm_nn <- emmeans::emmeans(lm_nn, ~ trtmnt_type)
# emm_nn

# pairwise contrasts
contrast_nn <- emmeans::contrast(emm_nn, method = "revpairwise", adjust = "tukey")
# contrast_nn

contrast_nn_df <- 
  summary(contrast_nn, infer = TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

# summary of pairwise differences
# pairwise_table <- 
  contrast_nn_df %>%
  dplyr::select(contrast, estimate, SE, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL, z.ratio, p.value) %>%
  kableExtra::kbl(
    caption = "pairwise mixed-model treatment comparisons for nearest neighbor tree distance (m)"
    , digits = 3
    , col.names = c(
      "contrast"
      , "nearest tree<br>difference estimate (m)"
      , "std. error"
      , "lower CL"
      , "upper CL"
      , "z-ratio"
      , "p-value"
    )
    , escape = F 
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling() %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general_title = "Interpretation:"
    , general = c(
      "difference estimate: positive values indicate the first treatment has wider tree spacing and vice-versa"
      , "confidence intervals (CL): if the interval includes 0, the difference is not statistically significant"
    )
  )
```

visualize that

```{r}
# plot pairwise contrasts
contrast_nn_df %>%

  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", lwd = 1.1) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbarh(
    ggplot2::aes(xmin = asymp.LCL, xmax = asymp.UCL)
    , height = 0.2, color = "gray33", size = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "navy", size = 3.5) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, breaks = scales::breaks_extended(n=6)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "pairwise treatment differences in nearest neighbor distance"
    # , subtitle = "mixed-model estimates with tukey adjusted 95% confidence intervals"
    , x = "estimated difference in nearest neighbor distance (m)"
    , y = ""
    , caption = "difference estimate: positive values indicate the first treatment has wider tree spacing and vice-versa"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_light() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(face="bold", size = 10)
    , panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

```

## Prescription Target Threshold Testing

Finally, let's perform a one-sided hypothesis test to determine if specific spacing targets were successfully met for the uniform treatments. Rather than comparing treatments to each other, this analysis evaluates each individual treatment's estimated marginal mean (accounting for both unit size and block variation) against the prescription tree spacing target. The null hypothesis is that the true average tree spacing is less than or equal to the target. A statistically significant upper-tail p-value (p < 0.05) provides evidence that a given treatment reliably met the prescription spacing target

```{r}
high_target_test <-
 emmeans::test(
   emm_nn
   , null = tree_obj_spacing_targets_df %>% dplyr::filter(trtmnt_type=="uniform- high") %>% dplyr::pull(target_nearest_dist_m)
   , side = ">"
  )
# high_target_test
low_target_test <-
 emmeans::test(
   emm_nn
   , null = tree_obj_spacing_targets_df %>% dplyr::filter(trtmnt_type=="uniform- low") %>% dplyr::pull(target_nearest_dist_m)
   , side = ">"
  )

target_df <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    dplyr::tibble(high_target_test) %>% dplyr::filter(trtmnt_type=="uniform- high")
    , dplyr::tibble(low_target_test) %>% dplyr::filter(trtmnt_type=="uniform- low")
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(trtmnt_type=as.character(trtmnt_type)) %>% 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tree_obj_spacing_targets_df %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(trtmnt_type=as.character(trtmnt_type))
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::relocate(trtmnt_type,target_nearest_dist_m)
```

summary table of one-sided hypothesis test to determine if specific spacing targets were successfully met for the uniform treatments

```{r}
target_df %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(target_nearest_dist_m,df)) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(
    caption = "hypothesis test: are block-adjusted tree spacings significantly greater than target spacing?"
    , digits = 3
    , col.names = c(
      "type"
      , "marginal mean<br>nearest neighbor distance (m)"
      , "std. error"
      # , "df"
      , "NULL:<br/>target spacing<br/>distance (m)"
      , "t-ratio"
      , "p-value"
    )
    , escape = F
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling() %>%
  kableExtra::footnote(
    general_title = "Interpretation:"
    , general = c(
      "marginal mean: the model-estimated average spacing controlling for unit size and block clustering"
      , "p-value: a small p-value (< 0.05) provides evidence the treatment met the spacing target"
    )
  )
```
